brief_definition.zh: 一种对记忆进行记录与保存的强烈欲望，以及与之共生的、潜在于归档行为中的对记忆的破坏与摧毁
brief_definition.en: A compulsive desire to record and preserve memory, with the inherent, latent destruction of that memory

zh: 1994年，在伦敦弗洛伊德博物馆——这位心理学大师生前的最后居所——雅克·德里达发表了关于“档案”的主题演讲。对德里达而言，这一场所深刻地影响了对“档案”的探讨：弗洛伊德的精神分析记录、档案，以及这一居所向“博物馆”的身份转型，都为讨论增添了多重维度。他敏锐地察觉到，“档案”与“精神分析”之间存在着复杂的联系，这种联系反映在私人与公共程序、制度、学术乃至法律的档案化过程之中。
在包括弗洛伊德在内的人类身上，德里达诊断出一种关于档案的“热病”（Archive Fever）。这是一种“强迫性的、重复且怀旧的欲望，表现为一种抑制不住的、试图回归源头的渴望；一种指向最古老、最绝对的发端场所的乡愁。”在当下，我们那些存满了聊天记录与生活碎片、容量庞大的云端硬盘，亦可被视为这种“热病”的表征。

德里达将这种“热病”与弗洛伊德提出的“死亡冲动”联系起来。正是由于对遗忘的恐惧，我们才建立档案，试图以此追寻那“绝对的起点”。然而，档案并非记忆本身，而仅是记忆的辅助器材，一种“义肢”（prosthetic）。它将原本“自然”且“内在”的记忆，寄存在可被阅读、复制的外部媒介（如纸张或硬盘）之上。因此，档案本身即是一个充满矛盾的概念：建立档案的前提恰恰是原生记忆的丧失与毁灭。可以说，档案在先验层面便是反对自身的。
在德里达看来，精神分析所构建的心理档案本质上也是一种“制度”与“建制”，标志着人类与自然状态的彻底决裂。由此，精神分析理论不仅是关于心理与记忆的学说，更演变成为一种关于档案的理论。
有趣的是，对德里达来说，档案并不只是关于“过去”的研究，更能影响未来。因为“归档行为”本身就在生产事件：档案的“技术底色”（technical substrate）预先决定了什么是“可被归档的”，进而反过来塑造了我们的生活经验。正如当下的短视频已经预设了特定的时长、画幅、记录逻辑与交互方式，这在很大程度上决定了未来的历史将以何种面貌呈现。
en: In 1994, at the Freud Museum in London—the psychoanalyst’s final residence—Jacques Derrida delivered a lecture on the "archive." For Derrida, this setting was more than a venue; it profoundly shaped his inquiry. Freud’s records and the transition of his home from a private residence to a museum added layers of meaning to the discussion. Derrida recognized a complex link between the archive and psychoanalysis, one that ripples through private and public programs and institutionalized process.

Derrida diagnosed a condition he called "Archive Fever" (Mal d'Archive) in many figures, including Freud. He described it as "a compulsive, repetitive, and nostalgic desire to return to the origin." Today, we see this "fever" manifest in our massive cloud drives, which overflow with years of chat logs, photos, apps, and other fragments of our lives.

Derrida linked this fever to Freud’s "death drive." The fear of forgetting compels us to build archives in the hope of recording a "starting point." Yet, the archive is not memory (mnēmē) itself; it is a prosthesis—a "hypomnesic" memory. It takes what was once "natural" and "internal" and consigns it to external, reproducible media like paper or hard drives. The archive is paradoxical: the very condition for its existence is the loss or destruction of the original, living memory. In this sense, the archive is "a priori, against itself."

For Derrida, psychoanalysis is itself a form of institutional archiving—a decisive break from a state of natural memory toward an external record of events. Consequently, psychoanalysis is not merely a study of the mind and memory; it becomes a theory of the archive itself.

example_sentence.zh: 每一顿饭他都拍照记录，这种档案热让他拥有了完美的数字记录，却也让他发现，如果没有手机里的照片，他甚至无法记起昨晚食物的味道。
example_sentence.en: He photographed every dish he had. While this archive fever left him with a perfect digital record, he eventually realized that without those photos, he couldn't even recall the taste of last night's dinner.

content.zh: 斯底德曼认为，“档案热”不仅是一种隐喻，也是一种真实的职业病，源于著名史学家儒勒·米什莱（Jules Michelet）由于多年在档案馆工作，吸入过多尘埃和病菌所导致的疾病。
content.en: Steedman argues that "archive fever" is not merely a metaphor but a genuine occupational disease, exemplified by the famous historian Jules Michelet, who fell ill after years of inhaling the dust and pathogens of the archives.

content.zh: 历史学家卡罗琳·斯底德曼（Carolyn Steedman）不完全认同德里达对“档案”的隐喻化解读，同时她提出了一种更为具体的“物质性”可能性。斯底德曼认为，“档案热”不仅是一种隐喻，也是一种真实的职业病，源于著名史学家儒勒·米什莱（Jules Michelet）由于多年在档案馆工作，吸入过多尘埃和病菌所导致的疾病。疾病源于“尘埃的物质存在，这些尘埃是动物躯体经历艰辛与磨难、成长与衰亡后残存的原子残骸。”这些尘埃在档案室中通过历史学家的研究和处理转变为其他形态，但从未真正消失。
content.en: Historian Carolyn Steedman does not fully subscribe to Derrida’s metaphorical reading of the "archive," proposing instead a possibility grounded in a more concrete "materiality." Steedman argues that "archive fever" is not merely a metaphor but a genuine occupational disease, exemplified by the famous historian Jules Michelet, who fell ill after years of inhaling the dust and pathogens of the archives. This malady stems from "the physical existence of dust, which is the atomic remains of animal bodies, their pain and their endurance, their growth and their decay." Through the historian’s research and handling, this dust is transmuted into other forms within the archive, yet it never truly vanishes.

content.zh:
有趣的是，对德里达来说，档案并不只是关于“过去”的研究，更能影响未来。因为“归档行为”本身就在生产事件：档案的“技术底色”（technical substrate）预先决定了什么是“可被归档的”，进而反过来塑造了我们的生活经验。正如当下的短视频已经预设了特定的时长、画幅、记录逻辑与交互方式，这在很大程度上决定了未来的历史将以何种面貌呈现。
我在想Sati的笔记中提到的“档案热”物质层面的可能性，这种灰尘和病菌，在数字档案中基本已经消失了，
content.en: Derrida argued that archiving is not just about the past—it dictates the future. The act of archiving actually produces the event as much as it records it. The "technical substrate" (the medium we use) predetermines what is "archivable," which in turn shapes our actual lived experience. Just as "reels" pre-determined the duration, framing, and modes of interaction for our lives, the technology of the archive decides what our  history will be.

brief_definition.zh: 提倡表面关注的诠释方法
brief_definition.en: brief

zh: 想象你坐在一个阳光明媚的公园长椅上，翻开一本诗集，不再绞尽脑汁地猜测诗人是否在隐喻社会不公或心理创伤，而是单纯地沉醉于文字的韵律、纸张的触感，以及诗句中描绘的蓝天白云——就像享受一杯清茶般纯粹。这种阅读方式，正是“表层阅读”的核心：它鼓励我们放下“侦探”般的猜疑，回归文本的可见表面。 表层阅读源于对传统文学批评方法的反思。在20世纪，主流批评如“症候阅读”（Symptomatic Reading）或“妄想阅读”（Paranoid Reading）要求读者扮演多疑的侦探，坚信文本背后隐藏着深层含义、意识形态或“症状”，必须挖掘出来才能揭示真相。例如，在分析一部小说时，批评家可能会过度解读一个角色的行为，将其视为资本主义压迫的象征。然而，表层阅读反对这种“深度挖掘”，转而强调文本的表面元素：包括语言的结构、字面意义、物质形式（如书籍的物理属性），以及显而易见的规律。它倡导一种“不带有妄想和猜忌”的阅读态度，旨在让读者从过度解读的负担中解放出来，在文学本身的享受中获得自由——就像在公园里，你不再为每片落叶赋予象征意义，而是单纯欣赏它的飘落之美。 这种方法并非否定深度，而是提醒我们：文本的表面同样丰富。它有助于避免主观臆断，促进更客观的文学分析，同时让阅读回归愉悦的本质。在数字时代，表层阅读还呼应了人们对信息过载的反思，鼓励我们慢下来，专注于眼前的内容。
en: extended

example_sentence.zh: 在讨论一部现代小说时，教授建议学生采用表层阅读的方法，专注于分析对话的节奏和场景描述的视觉细节，而不是急于推断作者的潜在政治立场。
example_sentence.en: example

content.en: abstract

content.zh: 我好奇的是表层阅读是否也有一套比较严格的方法——类似于“暂停怀疑”（suspension of skepticism)的阅读方法。事实上，究竟如何阅读应当是一个比较矛盾的过程，既有“不求甚解”也有“追根究底”可能才是最好的，我比较担心的是“表层阅读”像是一种情绪上的反弹：我累了，不想再当侦探了。我觉得这很真实，也很必要。但如果把它当成唯一正确的方法，那可能又走到了另一个极端。确实，过度的“分析解读”内在是一种控制欲，总想控制、揭露、占有意义，把文学当成了战斗对象。“表层阅读”强调回到语言本身、回到显现出来的样子，这在某种程度上是更“此在式”的，是一种愿意停下来、愿意被打动的阅读，这个态度值得学习，但象征、隐喻、深层意义恰恰是很多经典文本的生命力所在。

brief_definition.zh: 被忽视的、以情感关怀为核心的非标准化劳动群体。
brief_definition.en: brief

zh: 想象一下清晨的医院走廊。张护士长刚结束夜班，她不仅完成了输液、记录体征等“分内事”，更在一位焦虑的癌症患者床边多停留了半小时，握着他的手，听他倾诉对治疗的恐惧和家庭的担忧。她的眼神、语气和那份安静的陪伴，是药物之外的另一剂“良药”。这份工作记录表上无法量化、绩效考核难以体现的付出，正是“关怀阶级”劳动的缩影。 “关怀阶级”指的是那些在日常工作中，将大量时间和精力投入到对他人直接的、情感性的、非标准化的照料和支持中的劳动者群体。他们的核心价值不在于生产有形的商品或完成可精确计量的任务，而在于维系人际关系、提供情感支持、保障他人的基本福祉和尊严。这包括但不限于：基层服务人员（如社区工作者、养老护理员、幼儿教师）、大量从事辅助性工作的服务业人员（如文中提到的检票员），以及承担着繁重无偿家务和情感劳动的个体（尤其是女性）。 这类劳动常被主流经济模式所忽视或低估，因为它难以被标准化、流程化，其产出——如安全感、信任感、情感联结——不易被货币化衡量。然而，正是这些看似“无形”的关怀劳动，构成了社会运转和人日常生活的“情感脚手架”。它支撑着正式经济体系的运行（例如，家庭照护让其他成员能投入有偿工作），并直接关系到人的生活质量和社会凝聚力。 关注“关怀阶级”，旨在揭示和重新评估这类劳动的巨大社会价值，挑战以生产效率、GDP增长和标准化流程为核心的传统经济叙事。它呼吁社会政策和经济体系转向更重视人的实际福祉、互助关系和可持续性的公共经济模式，承认并支持这些维系社会基本温度的“关怀者”。
en: extended

example_sentence.zh: 部分批判性社会理论忽视"关怀", 认为"关怀"是私人，家庭领域的活动，缺乏政治性讨论的可能，是对积极行动和结构性变革的逃避，有去政治化的色彩。然而很多时候，"关怀阶级"营造了公共空间和公共变革的前提，也应当被重新思考。
example_sentence.en: example

content.zh: 导读
content.en: abstract

content.zh:
下层劳动者大量的工作是关心他人，而非机械的流水线生产。如，检票员大部分时间不在检票，而是指路、维护设施、寻找走丢的小孩、照顾老人、病人等。大量女性承担的家务牵扯情感、时间、精力，但并不在传统的“劳动”框架中。这样的关怀可能并不生产实际的“商品”或“有用之物”，却为商品的生产以及正式的劳动能够运行提供了基础。
        
关注“关怀阶层”，有助于突显更多人的劳动，以及大量被忽视的劳动时间和内容。与此同时，“关怀”与官僚和行政管理形成对比，后者更关注工作的标准化，而前者非标准化的工作落脚点在他人如何获益。关注“关怀”有助于摆脱以生产、消费、标准化效率为核心的经济模式，转向一种有益于人的实际互助福祉的公共经济。

brief_definition.zh: 现代化进程过快导致的高度压缩时空共存状况
brief_definition.en: brief

zh: 想象一下，你在玩一款城市模拟游戏，比如《模拟城市》。游戏中，你需要在短短几年内将一个小村庄发展成高科技大都市。你疯狂地建造工厂、摩天大楼和AI数据中心，但村庄里的老庙宇还没拆除，居民们一边用智能手机点外卖，一边参加传统祭祀活动，同时担心机器人会抢走他们的工作。这种混乱而快速的转型，就是压缩现代性的缩影——不同时代元素被硬生生挤进同一个时空里。 压缩现代性描述的是社会变迁中时间和空间被极度压缩的现象。当现代化进程过快时，前现代（如传统农业社会）、现代（如工业化城市）和后现代（如数字风险和全球化）元素被迫共存，形成一种流动而复合的体系。以韩国为例，它在20世纪后半叶仅用50年就完成了西方200-300年的工业化和经济增长，导致社会同时呈现发达国家的高科技、不发达国家的贫困问题以及独特的文化冲突。例如，首尔的年轻人可能一边追求个人主义（后现代），一边被家庭责任（前现代）束缚，同时面临经济不稳定（现代风险）。这种压缩性催生了“快文化”——结果主义、指标至上和效率优先，但也带来复合风险，如环境危机或社会分裂。张庆燮将这一概念扩展到东亚，中国改革开放的快速转型也类似：传统家庭价值观与现代个体主义交织，阎云翔等学者用它分析中国社会变迁。本质上，压缩现代性揭示了快速发展的代价：历史被折叠，社会在矛盾中前行。
en: extended

example_sentence.zh: 在巴西里约热内卢的贫民窟改造项目中，压缩现代性现象表现为原住民社区的传统手工艺与现代数字创业公司共存，居民们既参与古老节日庆典，又通过社交媒体推广业务，同时面临快速城市化带来的住房短缺问题。

content.zh: A large portion of the work performed by lower-class workers involves caring for others, rather than mechanical assembly-line production. For example, ticket inspectors spend most of their time not checking tickets, but giving directions, maintaining facilities, finding lost children, and caring for the elderly and the sick.  The domestic work performed by many women involves emotions, time, and energy, but it is not included in the traditional framework of "labor." This kind of care may not produce actual "goods" or "useful things," but it provides the foundation for the production of goods and the functioning of formal labor. Focusing on the "care sector" helps to highlight the labor of more people, as well as a large amount of overlooked labor time and content.  At the same time, "care" contrasts with bureaucracy and administrative management, which focus more on the standardization of work, while the non-standardized work of care centers on how others benefit. Focusing on "care" helps to move away from an economic model centered on production, consumption, and standardized efficiency, towards a public economy that benefits people through practical mutual aid and well-being.

brief_definition.zh: 处于过渡状态、模糊不清、缺乏具体功能或稳定身份的场域
brief_definition.en: A transitional, ambiguous state, lacking specific function or a stable identity

zh: 空旷的酒店走廊、楼梯间，或是夜晚安静的机场候机大厅，这些空间时常给人带来阴森和荒凉的感觉。它们本该是通往某个目的地的“中转站”，但当空无一人时，这些地方似乎成了失去社会属性和时间感的真空地带，变身为令人不安的过渡场所。

这种感觉正是“阈限空间”的典型体验。在拉丁语中，“Limen”意为“门槛”或“临界”。它指的是一种“介于两者之间”的过渡场所，是从事物现有状态向下一阶段转换的空间或时间。对人类学家范·根纳普（Arnold van Gennep）而言，仪式分为分离、过渡与融入三个阶段，而“阈限”正指向中间的过渡态——此时参与者已脱离了旧身份，却尚未获得新身份，处于一种模糊的、不确定的状态。维克多·特纳（Victor Turner）进一步深化了这一理论，他认为处于“阈限”中的人，如同掉进了社会结构的缝隙，暂时失去了原本的社会属性。当这种理论投射到物理空间时，那些原本作为“中转站”的楼梯间和候机厅，在空无一人时便失去了时间感与社会性，异化为令人不安的真空地带。
en: Think of an empty hotel hallway at 3 AM or a silent, cavernous airport terminal after the last flight has departed. These are places we usually pass through on our way to somewhere else in our daily lives. But when they are stripped of their usual bustle, it’s as if they’ve lost their sense of time and purpose, transforming into eerie, desolate unsettling transitional spaces.

This is the experience of a "liminal space." The term comes from the Latin limen, meaning "threshold." It describes the state of being "betwixt and between"—the physical or temporal gap where you have left one stage but haven't quite reached the next. Anthropologist Arnold van Gennep originally identified three stages of a rite of passage: pre-liminal (separation), liminal (transition), and post-liminal (incorporation). Liminality is the middle phase where a person is no longer who they were, but not yet who they will become.Turner expanded on the interstitial moment, where individuals exist on a threshold, temporarily stripped of social status, identity, and structure.

When applied to our physical world, these transitional zones—stairwells, parking lots, or closed shopping malls—become "liminal" when they are emptied of their social context, turning into haunting, dreamlike spaces that exist outside of normal reality.

example_sentence.zh: 对于很多在深夜还在地铁站徘徊的加班族来说，那座空旷、冰冷、充满回音的车站已不再是一个通勤节点，而是一个让他们在职场身份与家庭身份之间短暂喘息的阈限空间。
example_sentence.en: For many office workers wandering through a subway station late at night, the cavernous, cold, and echoing hall is no longer just a commuting node, but a liminal space that offers a brief respite between their professional identity and their domestic persona.

content.zh: 仔细看了一下4chan的原始帖子，很有意思：noclip是游戏里面类似于作弊模式的操作，字面意思是“不进行碰撞检测”。因此，玩家可以自由穿墙，然后到达很多游戏开发者本来不打算让玩家到达的地方。很明显，这个地方4chan用户对backroom“后室”的幻想，很大程度基于simulation一说——人类现实生活其实是高级文明创造的一场模拟。于是他讲，如果我们卡bug、穿墙，就能到达这些现实生活的“幕后空间”。很有意思的是大家不约而同都用阈限空间的场景来想象这些backroom——绵延不断的走廊、楼梯，交通空间，永远延伸下去，但又没有尽头。
content.en: "The original 4chan post is actually quite profound. It uses 'noclip'—a gaming cheat that literally means 'no collision detection'—as a metaphor. In a game, it lets you walk through walls and enter areas that aren't supposed to exist. It’s clear that the mythos of 'The Backrooms' is heavily based on Simulation Theory, the idea that our life is just a program run by a higher intelligence. The idea is that if we 'glitch' through the walls of reality, we end up in these 'backstage' spaces. What's striking is how everyone naturally imagines these rooms as liminal spaces—those never-ending hallways and empty transit areas that just go on and on with no exit in sight."

content.zh: 卡迪夫大学的亚历山大-迪尔 (Alexander Diel) 和迈克尔-刘易斯 (Michael Lewis) 将“阈限空间”令人不安的性质归因于 "恐怖谷" (uncanny valley) 现象。这一术语通常用于那 些与人类不完全相似的人形物体，它们会引起人们的不安情绪。在这种情况下，看似熟悉但却与现实有微妙偏差的物理场所会产生典型的边缘空间的阴森感。

brief_definition.zh: 清晰且必要的心理边界
brief_definition.en: A distinct and indispensable psychological boundary.

zh: 大年初三的客厅里，电视机里春晚的回放成了背景音。亲戚们围坐在茶几旁，剥着橘子，话锋一转指向了正在剥核桃的你：“还没谈对象吗？隔壁王阿姨的小孩都买房了。” 你感到一种熟悉的、如同被蛛网缠绕般的窒息。这种干涉往往披着“为你好”的外衣，却像是一场越界的入侵。在心理学上，打破这种窒息感的关键，就是“课题分离”。
这一概念由个体心理学的奠基人阿德勒提出。他认为，几乎所有的人际关系矛盾都源于对他人课题的妄加干涉，或者自己的课题被他人干涉。要判断一个课题属于谁，只需看“这个选择的后果最终由谁承担”。父母干涉子女的择偶，其实是把“子女的人生后果”错当成了自己的KPI；而子女因为父母的焦虑而感到愧疚，则是承担了本不属于自己的情绪责任。
阿德勒的主张诞生于20世纪初的奥地利，那正是现代个体主义蓬勃发展的时期。但在深受儒家文化影响、强调“血缘共同体”的东亚社会，这种边界感往往被视为冷漠。实际上，课题分离并非要切断联系，而是要把这种纠缠不清的“乱麻”梳理成平行的细线。只有当你意识到“我的选择权属于我，而你的失望属于你”时，真正的理解与尊重才有可能发生。它是人际关系的起点，只有建立在独立人格之上的关心，才不至于成为彼此的重担。
en: It is the third day of the Lunar New Year. The background noise of the television reruns fills the living room. Relatives circle the coffee table, peeling oranges, when the conversation suddenly shifts toward you: "Still single? The neighbor’s child just bought an apartment." You feel a familiar, web-like suffocation. This interference, often disguised as "good intentions," is an invasion of your psychological territory. In psychology, the key to breaking this deadlock is what Alfred Adler calls the "Separation of Tasks."

This concept, a cornerstone of Individual Psychology, posits that almost all interpersonal conflicts arise from the uninvited intrusion into others' tasks or having one's own tasks intruded upon. To identify the owner of a task, one must ask: "Who ultimately bears the consequences of this choice?" When parents interfere in a child's marriage, they are treating the child's life outcomes as their own performance indicators. Conversely, when individuals feel guilty for their parents' anxiety, they are assuming an emotional responsibility that is not theirs to carry.

Adler’s theory emerged in early 20th-century Austria during the rise of modern individualism. However, in East Asian societies influenced by Confucianism and the concept of a "blood-line community," this boundary is often misconstrued as coldness or alienation. In reality, the separation of tasks is not about cutting ties; it is about untangling a knotted mess into parallel threads. True understanding and respect only emerge when you realize: "My choice belongs to me, and your disappointment belongs to you." It is the starting point of healthy relations—a connection built on independent personality rather than mutual entanglement.

example_sentence.zh: 面对老板无理的情绪宣泄，她深吸一口气，利用课题分离告诉自己：努力工作是我的课题，而管理情绪是老板自己的课题。
example_sentence.en: Within an organization lacking effective management, the laxity of regulations often leads to an increase in administrative entropy, eventually plunging the department's operations into total disarray.

brief_definition.zh: 揭示物质真相的机械之眼
brief_definition.en: A mechanical gaze revealing material truths.

zh: 1929年的莫斯科街头，电车疾驰，人群如潮水般涌动。你正透过一片矩形的玻璃观察这一切。突然，世界在你面前被“拆解”又“重组”：路人的步伐被无限放慢，连靴底摩擦尘土的细节都清晰可见；下一秒，镜头飞越城市，将一个乞丐的倦容与工厂齿轮的轰鸣剪辑在一起。这不是梦境，而是“电影眼”在接管你的感官。它冷峻地宣告：人类的肉眼是软弱且充满偏见的，而摄像机的镜头——这只“机械之眼”——才是永不疲倦的真理探寻者。
吉加·维尔托夫发起的这场非虚构影像革命，核心在于对“肉眼”的祛魅。他认为电影不该是戏剧的拙劣模仿，也不应服务于虚构的故事。相反，摄像机应当像一把手术刀，切开日常生活的表象。通过蒙太奇，时间可以被逆转，空间可以被折叠，原本在肉眼中稍纵即逝、毫无关联的碎片，在胶片的拼接中显现出了社会的本质逻辑。
在《持摄影机的人》中，维尔托夫向我们展示了这种理想：电影不再是窗户，而是一件工具。它将目光投向街车、工人和机器的轰鸣，试图在工业文明的秩序中寻找一种“诗意的工业感”。这种将艺术政治化的尝试，本质上是希望通过机器的客观性，消除艺术与生活的隔阂，让每一个普通人都能通过镜头，看清自己所处的世界真相。
en: On the streets of Moscow in 1929, trams surge by and crowds flow like a rising tide. You are observing this chaos through a rectangular pane of glass. Suddenly, the world is deconstructed and reassembled before your eyes: the gait of a passerby is slowed to an infinite crawl, making the friction between boot and dust visible in crystalline detail. A second later, the lens leaps across the city, juxtaposing the weary face of a beggar with the rhythmic roar of factory gears. This is not a dream; it is the "Kino-eye" taking over your senses. It coldly proclaims: the human eye is weak and prejudiced, but the camera lens—this "mechanical eye"—is the untiring seeker of truth.

The non-fiction cinematic revolution initiated by Dziga Vertov was fundamentally a "disenchantment" of the human gaze. He argued that cinema should not be a mediocre imitation of theater, nor should it serve the whims of fictional storytelling. Instead, the camera should act as a scalpel, slicing through the surface of daily life. Through montage, time can be reversed, and space can be folded. Fragments that seem fleeting or unrelated to the naked eye reveal the profound underlying logic of society once stitched together on film.

In Man with a Movie Camera, Vertov demonstrates this ideal: cinema is no longer a window, but a tool. It directs its gaze toward streetcars, workers, and the roar of machines, seeking a "poetic industrialism" within the order of industrial civilization. This attempt to politicize art was, at its core, a hope that the objectivity of the machine could dissolve the barrier between art and life, allowing every ordinary person to see the truth of the world they inhabit through the lens.

example_sentence.zh: 虽然今天的运动相机和无人机视角已经极其普及，但它们大多只是为了追求视觉刺激，缺乏维尔托夫那种试图通过电影眼来重构社会秩序的野心。
example_sentence.en: While modern action cameras and drone perspectives have become ubiquitous, they often merely pursue visual stimulation, lacking Vertov’s radical ambition to reconstruct social order through the Kino-eye.

content.zh: 我来啦！我最初通过学习人类学领域的感官民族志 sensory ethnography 接触到这个概念，深深得益于这种突破既定模式的看见，也希望我的创作可以如此地打破常规。后来这个词也促使我多多了解苏联电影，了解苏联电影创作从自在到受限的历史。我发觉社会/科技/语言都作为系统，以一种难以被觉察的方式束缚我们的看见。创作者该如何一层层地，打破既定语言，电影技术，和“不可抗力”的束缚？这是我一直在思考的问题…

电影《攻壳机动队》中创造赛博格的场景。

content.en: abstract

content.zh:
之前在沙丘研究所上发过一篇文章，是关于押井守导演的两部《攻壳机动队》的。这里选了一段和“赛博格”相关的内容分享：

持续的网络化将我们带向一种极端程度的生物躯体与意识的脱离（disembodiment），这会从根本上改变了我们对人类的定义。
海尔斯在《我们何以成为后人类》 （#How We Became Posthuman#） 第一章中提到了笛卡尔经典的身心二元论，她认为这一哲学模型在当今时代正面对一些问题。譬如以下两个思维实验案例：第一，由汉斯·莫拉维克（Hans Moravec）提出的通过电脑下载可以获得的人类意识；第二，星际迷航系列电影中的瞬移机器。这两种当下科幻作品中热门的技术想象都对笛卡尔的身心二元论提出了扩充性的挑战。

身心二元论也是 #攻壳机动队# 系列无法避过的哲学主题。作品的片名“#Ghost in the Shell#”中的“ghost（灵魂）”即指意识和精神，而它是存在于“shell（躯壳）”即身体中的。在这一主线的引导下，海尔斯将“脱离生物基质”作为后人类的要素。海尔斯提出后人类将”身体视为原始的假肢/义体”，因此对它进行替换，改造和延展是自然而正常的。在这种视角下，赛博格就是完美的后人类范式。
在《赛博宣言》中，哈拉维将“赛博格的意象”视作“一种走出二元迷宫的方式”。“赛博格”对于哈拉维是一个抽象或隐喻的概念。在哈拉维看来，离体，或者说离体的意象，是人类达到理想的社会和政治环境的解放力量。
押井守在1995年的电影中对“认识论问题及其与赛博范式的关系”很感兴趣。在 #攻壳机动队# 中，先进的赛博世界“从根本上颠覆了人类的本体论基础”。在这个未来的世界里，人类的身体被电子机械的部分不断取代和增强。在 #攻壳机动队# 中，所有的角色都被不同程度地进行了电子化改造。最常见的是电子脑，一种人类大脑的机械外壳，它可以接入网络，存储记忆和与他人交流。而秘书们则有一双机械的手，关节可以移位展开，这样手指可以分裂成更多个指尖，在工作时打字速度更快。
巴特植入了机械的眼睛，而素子更是只有生物脑的女性赛博格（gynoid）。这些角色在导演的刻画下是与我们相近的人的形象。他们的身份为电影设置了前提，即身体是可以在不改变主体身份的情况下进行改变、替换、和增强。在这种预设下，押井守有针对性地设置了挑战这一假设的人物和情节，重申了人的身份问题。
影片利用赛博格主角、她的同事和“反派”傀儡师，提供了不同程度的“离体性”。
户草代表了对赛博化的反抗，也代表了对传统的人与我们的社会关系的定义的坚持。作为义体化最少的角色，他象征了一种将我们原生的生物身体视为身份定义的观点。另外，他是一个已婚，并有年幼的女儿的父亲。这种基于亲属关系的家庭建构，使他成为我们传统的社会建构的代表，反抗整个“后人类”的设定。
另一方面，反面人物傀儡师作为一个获得意识的电脑程序，进一步向离体的方向推进，达到一种意识纯粹的非物质性。傀儡师从未拥有过身体却获得了意识的事实，不仅支持了人意识的非物质性，也说明意识并不局限于“人”。他提供了一个关于意识诞生的新故事，一个纯粹的虚拟的、没有任何身体或生物化身的意识诞生的故事。
正如素子在与傀儡师的对比中产生了对自己 “人类性”的质疑，这部电影是对我们如何用物质和个体性来定义人的探索。主角和反面角色代表了两个极端：一个是作为个体人类出生，但完全化身为机械躯体进入网络空间的赛博格，另一个是在信息海洋中诞生的个体意识。

赛博格，可以被简单理解为肉身和人造科技混合的生命体。
我们不妨从这两个问题开始：虽然没有镭射眼或者手臂上的螳螂刀，但你真的完全不依赖人工科技来增强自己的生命体吗？赛博格乍看是一个带有强烈科幻色彩的词，但事实上，隐形眼镜、降噪耳机、防尘口罩、心脏起搏器、义肢等等，都已经是许多人生活中必不可少的“增强装置”了。手机、电脑等外部设备也同样在帮助我们增强记忆和通讯的能力。从这个角度看来，或许地球上大多数人已经可以被看做是赛博格。
第二，如果女性赛博格在体力、速度、力量都不再弱于男性，或者经过改造之后，不仅女性才有生育的能力，我们的社会性别又会怎么样定义？我们可以想象，很多“男性适合做什么，女性不擅长做什么”的传统说法会自动消散。
在能够通过技术手段打破生理限制的社会中，二元对立的性别观念的社会建构性质得以被重新审视。这种技术进步不仅可能消除性别之间的生理差异，还可能重新塑造我们对于能力、角色和身份的期望。从哈拉维的角度看，赛博格理论提供了一种解放性的视角，挑战既定的性别规范，开启对平等和多样性更深层次的探讨。

brief_definition.zh: 一种被法律与宗教共同抛弃、仅保留生理性存续的赤裸生命。
brief_definition.en: An entity doubly excluded from both legal and religious orders, possessing only a biological persistence known as "bare life."

zh: 想象一个被关押在没有国籍、没有编号、也不受任何国际法保护的“黑狱”中的囚犯。守卫可以对他施加任何暴力而无需承担法律责任，因为在法律眼中他并不存在；同时，他也不能像一个烈士或罪人那样被正式地处决或献祭，因为他被认为是不洁的，连神灵也不屑于接收他。他成了一个纯粹的、活着的肉块，游荡在文明的缝隙里。
这便是古罗马法中定义的“牲人”。意大利哲学家阿甘本通过这个概念，向我们展示了权力的阴暗面：主权（Sovereign）之所以强大，正是因为它有权宣布谁是“例外”。当一个人被宣布为“牲人”时，他就进入了一种“赤裸生命”（Bare Life）的状态。他被剥夺了公民身份、政治权利和宗教庇护，成为了一个“可以被杀死，但不能被祭祀”的存在。
阿甘本指出，这种状态并不是古代的遗迹，而是现代政治的底色。从集中营的受难者到现代城市中失去证件的非法移民，当法治社会宣布进入“例外状态”时，任何人都可能在瞬间被剥夺掉那一层名为“权利”的外衣，退化为仅仅在生物学意义上存活的“牲人”。这种排斥本身，正是主权确立其绝对权威的手段。
en: Imagine a prisoner held in a "black site"—without nationality, without an identification number, and existing entirely beyond the protection of any international law. A guard could inflict any degree of violence upon him without legal consequence, for in the eyes of the law, he does not exist as a legal subject. Yet, he cannot be formally executed as a criminal or offered as a martyr in a ritual sacrifice; he is deemed "impure," and even the divine refuses to claim him. He has become a mere vessel of living flesh, drifting through the cracks of civilization.

This is the definition of Homo Sacer in ancient Roman law. Through this concept, Italian philosopher Giorgio Agamben reveals the dark underbelly of power: sovereignty derives its strength precisely from its authority to declare the "exception." When an individual is designated as Homo Sacer, they enter a state of "bare life" (nuda vita). Stripped of citizenship, political agency, and religious sanctuary, they become a being that "may be killed but not sacrificed."

Agamben argues that this state is not a relic of antiquity but the very blueprint of modern politics. From the victims of concentration camps to undocumented migrants in contemporary metropolises, once a society declares a "state of exception," any individual can be stripped of the protective mantle of "rights" in an instant, regressing into the purely biological survival of the Homo Sacer. This exclusion is not a failure of the system, but the very mechanism by which sovereignty establishes its absolute authority.

example_sentence.zh: 在某些战乱地带，被炸毁家园且失去难民身份的人们，正处于一种牲人式的处境：他们在炮火中像草芥一样死去，却甚至无法在任何官方的伤亡名单上留下名字。
example_sentence.en: In certain war-torn territories, families who have lost both their homes and their refugee status exist in a Homo Sacer-like condition: they perish in the crossfire like blades of grass, yet their names are never recorded on any official casualty list.

content.zh:
homo sacer 译作‘神圣人’确实容易产生歧义——毕竟在意涵上面Homo Sacer正是不能用于献祭，所以恰恰在宗教上是不神圣的。这个词毫无疑问是阿甘本最重要的几个概念之一，我们在此处也希望提供一些基于现代社会的例子，方便大家理解。当然，沙丘的两位主理人并不是哲学或者政治哲学的背景，所以这部分举例也是基于“编舟记共创会”上大家的讨论和联想——首先是一些现实生活中的例子，如果在概念上和“牲人”并不相合，也欢迎大家指出和讨论：
1. 纳粹统治下的犹太人
2. “红色高棉时期”在柬埔寨被怀疑为资本主义者、知识分子、有外国联系的人
3. 从内乱的非洲国家逃往欧洲，漂在海上的难民和无国籍人士
4. 被美军视作恐怖分子嫌疑人，于是无限期拘留在关塔那摩湾，且不给予基本法律保护的囚犯

我也联想到了一些虚构创作中的例子：
1. 科幻电影《第九区》里面被隔离在特定区域的外星难民，被视为次等生命，可以被任意剥削和掠夺
2. 科幻电影《银翼杀手》中的复制人，他们在法律上没有人权，被视为生产工具。尽管在外观、情感和智力上与人类无异，他们的生命仍然可以被任意剥夺
3. 《饥饿游戏》当中被选中参与“饥饿游戏”的选手，生命可以在全国电视上被合法地剥夺

brief_definition.zh: 日益增长的系统混乱度量
brief_definition.en: An ever-increasing measure of systemic disorder.

zh: 你手里握着一杯温热的咖啡，脚下一滑，瓷杯在瓷砖地上摔得粉碎。深色的液体四溅，碎片铺满了地板。在这个瞬间，你见证了宇宙最核心的真理：复原那杯咖啡是不可能的。你可以打扫碎片，但你无法让瓷片自动跳回手中，更无法让热量重新聚集。这种从有序走向无序、从集中走向消散的单行道，就是“熵”。
从热力学的角度看，熵是能量退化的标尺。克劳修斯发现，在一个孤立的系统里，热量总是自发地从高温流向低温，这个过程产生的“熵”只会增加。这就像是宇宙的“燃料”在不断变成无法再利用的“废渣”。中文里“熵”字的设计非常精妙，它代表了“热量除以温度”的商，揭示了能量在转化中那种无可挽回的耗散。
而在统计物理学中，玻尔兹曼赋予了它更具象的含义：无序。想象一盒整齐排列的红墨水和蓝墨水，一旦撤掉隔板，分子们便开始疯狂且随机地跳舞。它们混合成紫色并非因为某种魔力，而是因为“混乱”的状态数远多于“整齐”的状态数。熵增，本质上就是系统向“最有可能出现的混乱状态”演进的概率游戏。
到了信息时代，香农将这一概念引入通信。如果一条消息毫无悬念，那它的熵就是零；越是出乎意料的消息，蕴含的信息熵就越高。熵在这里，变成了对“不确定性”的精准称重。
en: Imagine you are holding a cup of warm coffee. Your foot slips, and the ceramic mug shatters against the tiled floor. Dark liquid splashes everywhere, and shards of porcelain scatter across the room. In this fleeting moment, you have witnessed one of the most fundamental truths of the universe: restoring that cup of coffee is an impossibility. You can sweep up the shards, but you cannot command the pieces to leap back into your hand, nor can you force the dissipated heat to reconcentrate. This one-way street—leading from order to disorder, from concentration to dissipation—is what we call "entropy."

From a thermodynamic perspective, entropy is the yardstick of energy degradation. Rudolf Clausius discovered that in an isolated system, heat always flows spontaneously from hot to cold; the "entropy" produced by this process only ever increases. It is as if the "fuel" of the universe is being constantly converted into unusable "exhaust." The Chinese character "熵" (shāng) is ingeniously designed: it combines the radical for "fire/heat" (火) with the character for "quotient" (商), representing the mathematical ratio of heat divided by temperature, thereby revealing the irrevocable dissipation inherent in energy transformation.

In statistical physics, Ludwig Boltzmann gave this concept a more tangible meaning: disorder. Imagine a container with red and blue ink neatly separated by a partition. Once the partition is removed, the molecules begin a frantic, random dance. Their eventual mixing into a uniform purple is not due to some mysterious force, but because the number of "disordered" states vastly outnumbers the "ordered" ones. Entropy, at its core, is a game of probability where the system evolves toward the most likely state of chaos.

By the information age, Claude Shannon introduced this concept to communication. If a message contains no surprises, its entropy is zero; conversely, the more unexpected a message is, the higher its "information entropy" becomes. In this context, entropy has become a precise scale for weighing "uncertainty."

example_sentence.zh: 在一个缺乏有效管理的组织内部，规章制度的松懈往往会导致行政效能的熵增，最终使得部门运作陷入彻底的混乱。
example_sentence.en: Within an organization lacking effective management, the laxity of regulations often leads to an increase in administrative entropy, eventually plunging the department's operations into total disarray.

content.zh: “熵”这个中文汉字其实也是一个非常晚近的发明，是中国物理学家严济慈于20世纪50年代创造的。严济慈在翻译克劳修斯的热力学著作时，需要为“entropy”找到一个合适的中文词汇。他考虑到熵的定义是“热量除以温度”，所以选择了“熵”这个字。这个字是从“热”的偏旁和“商”的读音结合而来的，寓意“热量的商”。

brief_definition.zh: 借助互联网平台匹配供需的临时工作组成的经济领域，时间短、灵活但也缺乏福利和保障
brief_definition.en: An economic sector composed of temporary work matched through online platforms, characterized by short duration and flexibility but also lacking benefits and protections

zh: 零工是当下最迫切、最普遍的劳工状况。零工经济一个由互联网平台匹配供需的临时工作世界，时间短、灵活性强，却常伴随着福利缺失和职业不稳定，它尤其剥削原本就处于社会底层的劳工，包括低收入、低教育程度群体、女性等，但随着互联网和“接单”式工作成为主流，大量曾经的白领工作也逐渐“零工化”。

零工经济并非21世纪的新产物。早在三百年前，欧洲的艺术家就承接“独立计件合同”，类似今天的自由职业；中国乡土社会的农忙“短工”，也是其历史雏形。但数字技术的崛起重塑了这一模式：平台App（如网约车软件或闲鱼）取代了传统的熟人介绍或集市匹配，将出行、外卖、设计甚至剧本写作等产业“零工化”。这带来了双重效应：一方面，它为个体（如失业建筑师或学生）开辟了灵活收入渠道，经济学家赞其为“解放朝九晚五的枷锁”；另一方面，平台算法主导的派单和评分机制，往往将零工者推向“丛林竞争”——低价抢单、缺乏职业成长空间，且难以形成工会或行业规范。本质上，零工经济是社会原子化的数字表现：工作者被降级为可替换的“零件”，而平台垄断话语权，加剧了经济不平等。
en: Gig work is currently the most pressing and widespread labor situation. The gig economy is a world of temporary work facilitated by internet platforms that match supply and demand.  While it offers short-term work and flexibility, it often comes with a lack of benefits and job insecurity. It particularly exploits workers already at the bottom of the social ladder, including low-income individuals, those with low levels of education, and women. However, as the internet and "on-demand" work become mainstream, a large number of previously white-collar jobs are also gradually becoming "gigified."

example_sentence.zh: 上门绘图的兴起或许帮助收入下降的建筑师群体解决短期的财务焦虑，但这种"零工经济"造成的低价竞争可能会对行业造成更为长远的伤害。
example_sentence.en: The rise of on-site drawing services may help architects experiencing a drop in income address short-term financial anxiety, but the low-cost competition created by this 'gig economy' could cause more long-term damage to the industry.

content.zh: 在卡尔·波兰尼的《大转型》一书中，pauperism（贫民化）是英国工业转型中最明显的社会问题，波兰尼指出，随着工厂资本主义发展，出现了伪商品（Fictitious Commodity）：土地、人的生命、货币都不应该作为商品存在，却被变成了商品。在数字时代，平台经济似乎重现了一些fictitious commodity: 劳动、时间、注意力。波兰尼认为劳动力本质上是人类生命活动，而非为市场而生的商品。当平台通过算法将鲜活的人还原为可随时调取、按秒计价的“运力单位”时，这种强制的伪商品化逻辑重现了，它的商品交易掩盖了残酷的现实：算法在剥离了社会保险与法律责任的同时，也剥夺了劳动者作为“社会人”的稳定性。它虽然创造了极具灵活性的劳动力市场，却以摧毁人的社会尊严与生存韧性为代价。
content.en: In Karl Polanyi’s The Great Transformation, pauperism stands as the most conspicuous social wreckage of the English industrial transition. Polanyi contends that the rise of industrial capitalism necessitated the invention of fictitious commodities: land, labor, and money—elements that are fundamentally not produced for sale, yet are treated as if they were. In the digital era, the platform economy resurrects this fiction by commodifying not just labor, but time and attention itself. Since labor is merely another name for a human being’s life activity, its reduction by algorithms into 'on-demand units' or 'per-second logistics' represents a radical re-commodification. This market fiction veils a grim reality: by stripping away social protections and legal accountability, the algorithm eviscerates the stability of the 'social man.' It yields a hyper-flexible labor market at the catastrophic cost of human dignity and social resilience.

brief_definition.zh: 包含有两个相反意思的词或者字
brief_definition.en: A word that encompass two contradictory meanings

zh: 中文里，“置”有抛弃、废弃的意思，比如“置之不理”、“置于一旁”。但“置”也有操办、营造的意思，比如“安置”、“布置”、“置办”等等，这就使得这一个汉字带有近乎自相矛盾的两种含义。
英文中也有不少这样的例子，比如“ravel”有解开、理顺的意思，但也有缠结、使…错综复杂的意思。俚语也会导致这样的情况，比如迈克尔·杰克逊的专辑（和单曲）Bad 意思并不是太坏了、太糟了，而是很厉害、不好惹。
这些字或词即是反训词（contronym，或者Auto-antonym，也译作‘自反意语’），或者双面词（Janus words - Janus是罗马神话里的雅努斯双面神）。
en: In Chinese, for example, the character zhi (置) carries nearly contradictory senses. It can mean to abandon or ignore, like in the phrase "to leave something aside," but it can also mean to arrange or set up, as in "to furnish" or "to organize."

English is no stranger to this phenomenon. The word ravel, for instance, can mean to straighten out threads or to tangle them up. Slang further contributes to this, such as when Michael Jackson used the word Bad to mean "cool" or "tough" rather than "poor quality."
These are called contronyms (or auto-antonyms), and are often nicknamed Janus words after the Roman god who had two faces looking in opposite directions.

example_sentence.zh: 中文中，“大败”既有战胜、击败的意思，也有落败、被打败的意思。
example_sentence.en: In Latin, the word hospes carries the twofold meaning of "guest" and "host." In English, dust is a curious example of a word that can mean both to sprinkle something on and to wipe something away.

content.zh: 对于阿甘本的著作，中文译本可以找到“神圣人”和“牲人”两种用语。
content.en: In the Chinese editions of Giorgio Agamben’s works, two distinct renderings can be found: Shengsheng Ren (Sacred Man) and Sheng Ren (The Expendable/Sacrificial Man).

content.zh:
我们探讨过“homo sacer”这个词的译法问题。对于阿甘本的著作，中文译本可以找到“神圣人”和“牲人”两种用语。

在推送发出后，我们的好友安太然补充提醒我们，拉丁语中的sacer本就是一个典型的“contronym”（反训词），兼有“神圣的、不可触碰的”和“臭名昭著的、被诅咒的”两重意思。可能这也是为什么“homo sacer”一词的译法存在如此多有趣的争议。

我们借上这个由头，今天的推送就简单介绍“反训词”，并捎带上“反义复词”这个概念。当然，“反义复词”一般用在汉语的分析当中，英文中的相关词语是我们个人延伸出的，将它们称作“反义混成词”应该更为恰当。
content.en:
We previously explored the translation of the term homo sacer. In the Chinese editions of Giorgio Agamben’s works, two distinct renderings can be found: Shengsheng Ren (Sacred Man) and Sheng Ren (The Expendable/Sacrificial Man).
Following our previous post, our friend An Tairan added a insightful reminder that the Latin word sacer is itself a quintessential contronym. It encompasses the dual meanings of "sacred/inviolable" and "infamous/accursed." This inherent ambiguity likely explains why the translation of homo sacer remains a subject of such intriguing debate.
Taking this as a starting point, today’s post will briefly introduce the concept of contronyms, along with the notion of antonymous compounds. While the latter is typically used in the analysis of the Chinese language, we have personally extended this logic to English. It would perhaps be more appropriate to refer to these English equivalents as antonymous portmanteaus.

content.zh: 有几个成语是我在搜索反训词的相关知识的时候联想到的，几个好友也有补充：“差强人意”，原本的意思是“大体上能够让人满意”，但经常被误用为相反的意思。“万人空巷”，原本指的是人挤人的热闹盛况，很多时候被误用作相反的意思，“街上没人”。最好笑的应该是“空穴来风”，自相矛盾的两个意思已经写在现代汉语词典里了：原本比喻“传言有所依据”，现在用来指“传言没有依据”。这些词再这样用下去，可能已经起不到交流的作用了…
content.en:
While researching contronyms, several Chinese idioms came to mind—some also suggested by friends. For instance, cha qiang ren yi (差强人意) originally meant "largely satisfactory," yet it is frequently misused to convey the exact opposite. Then there is wan ren kong xiang (万人空巷), which describes a bustling scene where everyone has poured out of their homes to throng the streets; ironically, it is often misinterpreted to mean "empty streets with no one in sight."
Perhaps the most amusing case is kong xue lai feng (空穴来风). The two contradictory meanings are now both officially recorded in modern Chinese dictionaries: while it originally alluded to "rumors having a factual basis," it is now commonly used to mean "rumors with no basis at all." If we continue to use these words in such a manner, they may eventually lose their function as a medium for communication altogether...

content.zh: 不知道算不算反训词相关现象，不过 fact 来自 拉丁文 factum 意思是「人做的一件事或者制作的一个东西」，后面衍生出事实（fact）和虚假（factitious）这两个方向的含义
content.en: I am not certain if this strictly qualifies as a contronym-related phenomenon, but the word fact originates from the Latin factum, meaning "a thing done" or "a thing made." Interestingly, it evolved into two divergent semantic directions: fact, representing objective reality, and factitious, which denotes something artificial or false.

brief_definition.zh: 一对单音反义词结合起来构成的一个新词
brief_definition.en: A word formed by the combination of a pair of monosyllabic antonyms

zh: 中文里有很多由相反意思汉字组成的两字词，比如“多少”、“好歹”、“褒贬”、“沉浮”、“巨细”、“天地”等。
这些词中很多是偏义复词，即偏重这两个意思中的其中一个：比如“谁主沉浮”，偏向浮，“不计得失”，偏重失。有些词以相反的两个点为基础，指的是这之间的整个事物，比如“天地”。也有一些用来比喻或者提喻其他事物，比如用“手足”指代兄弟，“开关”提喻电子器械的点按装置。
英文中的合成词（compound）或混成词（blend words）中也有一些是由意义相反的词直接组合而成的。比如“bittersweet”（bitter+sweet，悲喜交集），口语上说的“frenemy”（friend+enemy，亦敌亦友）。这些词的含义就是两个组成部分的混合。
不过也有一些历史更古老的词也是由两个相反的词拼成，但带有其组成部分之外的含义。比如“sophomore”这个词，意思则是“大学二年级的学生”。
en: The Chinese language contains many disyllabic words composed of antonymic characters, such as "much and little" (duōshǎo 多少), "good and bad" (hǎodài 好歹), "praise and criticism" (bàobiǎn 褒贬), "rise and fall" (chénfú 沉浮), "magnitude" (jùxì 巨细), and "heaven and earth" (tiāndì 天地).

Many of these are partial-meaning compounds (偏义复词), where the emphasis is placed on only one of the two components. For instance, in the phrase "Who governs the rise and fall" (谁主沉浮), the weight is on "rise" (fú 浮); in "regardless of gain or loss" (不计得失), the focus is on "loss" (shī 失).

Other terms use two opposing poles to represent an entire spectrum, such as "heaven and earth" (天地) denoting the universe. Some function as metaphors or synecdoches (提喻), such as using "hands and feet" (手足) to refer to brothers, or "on and off" (开关) as a synecdoche for the toggling mechanism of electronic devices.

Similar constructions exist in English through compound words or blends. We see this in "bittersweet" (a fusion of bitter and sweet) and the colloquial "frenemy" (friend and enemy), where the meaning is a direct blend of both parts.

However, some etymologically ancient words are also composed of opposites but carry a significance beyond their literal parts. A prime example is "sophomore" (a second-year student), which originates from the Greek roots sophos ("wise") and moros ("foolish")—rendering the literal but hidden meaning of a "wise fool."

example_sentence.zh: 中文中的反义复词和英文中的矛盾结合词（Oxymoronic Compound）既有共性又有差异，比如英文词sophomore（大学二年级学生）是后者的一个例子，它由希腊词根sophistēs（智慧、有经验的人）和mōros（傻子、白痴）混成；oximoron（矛盾修辞法）这个词本身也是一个例子，它由希腊语中的oxys（锐利的）和mōros（愚钝的）组成。
example_sentence.en: Antonymous compounds (fǎnyì fùcí 反义复词) in Chinese and oxymoronic compounds in English share both commonalities and distinct differences. For instance, the English word sophomore (a second-year college student) is a classic example of the latter; it is a blend of the Greek roots sophos (wise or experienced) and mōros (foolish or idiotic). The term oxymoron (a figure of speech that pairs contradictory terms) is itself another example, derived from the Greek words oxys (sharp/keen) and mōros (dull/stupid).

content.zh: 导读
content.en: abstract

content.zh:
“东西”一词可能是最常用的反义复词了——两个相反方位的并置，居然可以用来笼统代指大千世界的万事万物。一个比较常见的解释是说，唐朝的长安城内有两个主要的集市：东市和西市。当人们要获取、交换、购置商品，就要“上东市、上西市”，可能慢慢地，这在口语里就演化为了“买东西”，而这里的“东西”再从商品泛化到更广阔的的事物。
借着考究这个词，再看看其他语言中的情况。英语中的 Thing 和德语中的 Ding 都是来自在古诺斯语（þing）。它原本指的并不是物体，而是事件，是“集会、议事、讨论”，是有待裁决的议题。所以当一个日耳曼先民指着某个物件叫“Thing”时，他的潜台词其实是——“这是我们要开会讨论的那件事”。
法语中的Chose 和西班牙语 Cosa 也与之有相似性。它们来自拉丁语的 Causa，英语中的cause 是其后代。这个拉丁词原本的意思是“诉讼、案件、法律程序”。从这个意味上来说，拉丁语系的“东西”起始于那些需要在法庭上被争论的事物。
content.en:
The word "Dōng-xī" (literally "East-West") is perhaps the most ubiquitous antithetical compound in the Chinese language. It is a fascinating linguistic phenomenon where the juxtaposition of two cardinal directions serves as a catch-all term for the myriad "things" of the world. A common explanation traces this back to the Tang Dynasty, specifically to the two primary marketplaces in the capital of Chang’an: the East Market and the West Market. When people needed to acquire, exchange, or purchase goods, they had to "visit the East Market" or "visit the West Market." Over time, this likely evolved into the colloquialism "buying things" (mǎi dōng-xī), eventually generalizing from physical commodities to encompass all objects and affairs.
By using this etymological lens to examine other languages, we find similar patterns. The English word "Thing" and the German "Ding" both derive from the Old Norse þing. Originally, the word did not refer to a physical object, but to an event—a "meeting, assembly, or council"—an issue awaiting a verdict. Thus, when a Germanic ancestor pointed at an object and called it a "thing," the subtext was essentially: "This is the matter we are meeting to discuss."
The French Chose and Spanish Cosa share a similar lineage. They stem from the Latin Causa (the root of the English word "cause"). This Latin term originally signified a "lawsuit, a case, or a legal proceeding." In this sense, "things" in the Romance languages originated from matters that required debate within a court of law.

brief_definition.zh: 与外界没有因果联系的时空区域的边界面，常见于黑洞的表面
brief_definition.en: The boundary interface of a spacetime region that has no causal connection with the outside world is commonly found on the surface of a black hole.

zh: 想象一下，你正坐在一艘飞船里，不幸被一个巨大黑洞的引力捕获，正无可挽回地滑向它的中心。起初，你还能看到飞船仪表盘的光亮，也能看到远处未被黑洞吞噬的星光。但随着你越来越接近那个神秘的中心点，奇怪的事情发生了：你回头望向飞船的舷窗，试图看到你来的方向，却发现外面的星光似乎被拉长、扭曲，然后……消失了。你并非坠入了黑暗，而是到达了一个连光都无法向外逃逸的边界——事件视界。在这个边界之内，任何信息，包括你发出的求救信号、飞船引擎的亮光，甚至是你最后的一声叹息，都将永远无法被边界之外的宇宙所知晓。你与外部宇宙的因果联系，被彻底切断了。

在爱因斯坦的广义相对论中，物质和能量会使时空结构发生弯曲。当这种弯曲达到极致，比如在黑洞周围，就会形成一个特殊的边界——事件视界。它标志着时空中的一个临界点：在这个边界之内（朝向黑洞中心的方向），时空的弯曲是如此剧烈，以至于任何物体（包括以光速运动的光子）的未来路径都只能指向黑洞的中心奇点，而无法再折返或逃逸到边界之外。因此，视界内部发生的一切事件（如飞船解体、时间流逝），都无法以任何形式（信号、光线、引力波）影响到视界之外的外部宇宙。反之，外部宇宙也无法直接影响视界内部。它就像一个单向膜，只允许物质和信息进入，但禁止其逃出。虽然事件视界最常见于黑洞表面（被称为史瓦西半径），但理论上也可能存在于其他极端引力环境（如某些宇宙模型中的宇宙视界）。2019年，事件视界望远镜（EHT）合作项目发布的首张黑洞（M87星系中心）照片，其模糊光环的中心暗影区域，就大致对应着该黑洞事件视界的投影，让这个深奥的理论概念首次拥有了直观的视觉证据。
en: Imagine that you are sitting in a spaceship, unfortunately caught by the gravitational pull of a massive black hole and sliding inexorably towards its center. At first, you can still see the light on the spaceship's dashboard and the distant stars that haven't been devoured by the black hole. But as you get closer and closer to that mysterious center point, strange things happen: you look back at the spaceship's window, trying to see the direction you came from, but you find that the outside stars seem to be stretched, distorted, and then... disappear. You are not falling into darkness, but reaching a boundary where even light cannot escape - the event horizon. Within this boundary, any information, including your distress signals, the light from the spaceship's engine, and even your last sigh, will never be known by the universe beyond the boundary. Your causal connection with the external universe is completely severed.

In Einstein's general theory of relativity, matter and energy cause the structure of spacetime to bend. When this bending reaches its extreme, such as around a black hole, a special boundary is formed - the event horizon. It marks a critical point in spacetime: within this boundary (towards the center of the black hole), the curvature of spacetime is so intense that the future path of any object (including photons moving at the speed of light) can only point towards the black hole's central singularity, and cannot return or escape beyond the boundary. Therefore, all events that occur within the event horizon (such as the disintegration of the spaceship, the passage of time) cannot affect the external universe beyond the boundary in any form (signals, light, gravitational waves). Conversely, the external universe cannot directly affect the interior of the event horizon. It is like a one-way membrane that only allows matter and information to enter but prohibits their escape. Although the event horizon is most commonly found on the surface of a black hole (known as the Schwarzschild radius), theoretically it can also exist in other extreme gravitational environments (such as the cosmic horizon in certain universe models). In 2019, the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) collaboration project released the first image of a black hole (at the center of the M87 galaxy), with the dark shadow at the center of the blurry ring, roughly corresponding to the projection of this black hole's event horizon, giving this profound theoretical concept its first visual evidence.

example_sentence.zh: 在构思硬核科幻小说时，作者需要精确理解事件视界的物理含义：任何落入其中的角色或飞船，从宇宙的视角看，其命运在穿过边界的那一刻就已注定与外部世界彻底隔绝，任何信息都无法逃逸出来。

content.zh: 我试图理解了这个词，在物理学中，事件视界是信息无法逃逸的单向边界。很有趣的是，“horizon”一词不仅在物理学界被使用，在文学、文化研究等领域、以及日常口语中，horizon，地平线，也是一个经常被使用的描述预期以及无法预料的未来的词语。人类学家Ariana Petryna 在《Horizon Work》中恰恰捕捉到了类似的逻辑：当旧有的数据不再有用，当基于过去信息的预测变得具有误导性、甚至产生高昂的计算成本或不稳定性时，一个“新的预测视界（predictive horizon）”必须被确立 。比如人类在面对失控的气候变化时 。
content.en:
“Data from the past is useful, but only up to a point.
And precisely when data is no longer useful, and prediction
capability derived from past or present
information becomes
misleading (or yields high computational cost or instability), a
new predictive horizon must be put into place."

brief_definition.zh: 指源自潜意识层面的，由于压抑某些冲动和意图造成的，在言语、记忆或肢体动作上出现的失误行为
brief_definition.en: It refers to the mistakes in speech, memory or body movements that arise from the subconscious level due to the suppression of certain impulses and intentions.

zh: 想象一下，你正在参加一场重要的面试，面试官问起你的职业规划时，你本想自信地说“我渴望成为团队领导者”，却脱口而出“我害怕成为团队领导者”。这种看似简单的口误，在精神分析学中被称为“行为倒错”。它不只是日常的失误，而是潜意识中压抑的冲动或焦虑的短暂暴露。
弗洛伊德派理论认为，行为倒错源于本我（id）对自我（ego）的边界突破。当个体在道德或社会规范的压力下，压抑与性、暴力或创伤相关的欲望时，这些冲动会退入潜意识。但如果压抑不够牢固，它们就可能以口误、笔误、误听或暂时性遗忘的形式“泄露”出来。例如，在厨房做菜时叫错女友名字，可能暗示了未解决的过去情感。
英文术语“Parapraxis”源自希腊语前缀“Para”（意为“另一个”）和“Praxis”（意为“行动”），强调这是一种“替代性行为”。它与梦的机制相似，都是潜意识通过伪装方式表达真实意图。弗洛伊德在1901年的著作中，将这类现象视为通往潜意识的重要窗口，帮助我们理解人类心理的复杂性。行为倒错提醒我们，日常错误往往承载着深层心理冲突，而非单纯的疏忽。
en: Imagine that you are attending an important interview. When the interviewer asks about your career plan, you were about to confidently say "I aspire to be a team leader", but instead you blurted out "I'm afraid of being a team leader". This seemingly simple slip of the tongue is called "behavioral inversion" in psychoanalysis. It is not just a common mistake, but a brief exposure of repressed impulses or anxiety in the subconscious.

The Freudian theory holds that behavioral distortion stems from the boundary breach of the id (the primitive part of the psyche) over the ego. When an individual is under the pressure of moral or social norms and suppresses desires related to sex, violence, or trauma, these impulses retreat into the subconscious. However, if the suppression is not strong enough, they may "leak" out in the form of slips of the tongue, writing errors, mishearing, or temporary forgetfulness. For instance, calling one's girlfriend's name wrongly while cooking in the kitchen might imply unresolved past emotions.

The English term "Parapraxis" is derived from the Greek prefix "Para" (meaning "another") and "Praxis" (meaning "action"), emphasizing that it is a "substitute behavior". It is similar to the mechanism of dreams, both of which are ways for the subconscious to express true intentions through disguise. In his 1901 work, Freud regarded such phenomena as an important window to the subconscious, helping us understand the complexity of human psychology. Parapraxis reminds us that everyday mistakes often carry deep psychological conflicts rather than being simple negligence.

example_sentence.zh: 在婚礼致辞中，新郎本想感谢父母的养育之恩，却无意间说成了“感谢父母的养育之恨”，这被心理学家解读为一种典型的行为倒错，反映了潜意识中的家庭矛盾。
example_sentence.en: In the wedding speech, the groom intended to express his gratitude to his parents for their upbringing, but accidentally said "Thank you for your upbringing of me, but with resentment", which was interpreted by psychologists as a typical case of behavioral inversion, reflecting the latent family conflicts in his subconscious mind.

content.zh:
所有的“社死”时刻，本质上都是一场潜意识的武装起义。
在社交媒体构建的精密世界里，我们习惯了用“自我（Ego）”去精心维护一个体面、专业、情绪稳定的外壳。但“本我（Id）”从不休息，它像一个在后台运行却从未关闭的进程，一直在寻找防御的漏洞。而现在的智能输入法通过联想功能，某种程度上成为了我们潜意识的外部化器官。
那个发错群的吐槽、那个因手滑而点亮的赞，或许都是潜意识在表层意识上留下的暴力痕迹。在那一刻，那个被你压抑许久的、愤怒的、嫉妒的、或者仅仅是感到疲惫的“本我”，突然撕开了面具，发出一声响亮的尖叫。
“社死”之所以痛苦，是因为它强行打破了我们维持虚假秩序的幻觉。它在提醒你：即便你把自己包装得再像一个完美的社会生物，你的身体里依然跳动着一颗充满裂缝、不守规矩的人心。

brief_definition.zh: 新社会结构下的阶层概念，指从生产者社会走向消费者社会后，有缺陷的消费者
brief_definition.en: The concept of social classes in the new social structure refers to the flawed consumers who emerge after the transition from a producer-based society to a consumer-based society.

zh: 想象一下，一个名叫小张的年轻人，刚毕业就进入一家科技公司工作。他每月工资勉强够付房租和基本开销，但看到同事们都在炫耀新款的智能手机和周末的豪华旅行时，他感到一种无形的压力。一次公司聚餐，大家讨论着最新上市的电动汽车，小张只能默默低头——他连首付都凑不齐。这种无法参与“正常”消费的羞愧感，让他觉得自己像个局外人，尽管他勤奋工作，却总被贴上“不够成功”的标签。这就是“新穷人”的典型处境：在消费者社会中，他们不是饿肚子的人，而是消费能力不足的“缺陷者”。

这个概念源于社会结构的深刻转变。在工业革命时期的生产者社会里，工作伦理主导一切：人们被教育要勤劳、忠诚，像机器一样运转，不工作被视为道德败坏。穷人往往是那些“懒惰”或“散漫”的工人，社会用“有付出才有收获”的信念来驱使他们。但随着经济全球化，社会进化到消费者社会——这里，身份和阶级不再由工作能力定义，而是由消费选择自由决定。我们一生都在被训练成消费者：从广告到社交媒体，都在暗示“体面生活”的标准是买得起房、开好车、追潮流。新穷人就是那些无法达到这些标准的人，他们可能有一份工作，却因高物价、低工资或失业而消费受限。贫穷不再是生存威胁（如饥饿），而是一种社会心理排斥：无法消费意味着被边缘化，引发羞愧和负罪感。全球范围内，这种“新贫穷”在发达城市尤为明显，它提醒我们，消费主义如何重塑了不平等。
en: Imagine a young man named Xiao Zhang who just graduated and started working at a technology company. His monthly salary was barely enough to cover rent and basic expenses. But when he saw his colleagues showing off their new smartphones and enjoying luxurious weekend trips, he felt an invisible pressure. At a company dinner, everyone was discussing the newly launched electric vehicles. Xiao Zhang could only lower his head in silence - he couldn't even come up with the down payment. This shame of being unable to participate in "normal" consumption made him feel like an outsider, despite his hard work, he was always labeled as "not successful enough". This is the typical situation of the "new poor": in a consumer society, they are not the starving ones, but the "defective" ones with insufficient consumption capacity.

This concept stems from the profound transformation of social structure. In the producer society during the Industrial Revolution, work ethics dominated everything: people were educated to be diligent and loyal, to operate like machines, and not working was regarded as moral corruption. The poor were often those "lazy" or "disorganized" workers, and society used the belief that "paying the price leads to rewards" to drive them. However, with economic globalization, society has evolved into a consumer society - here, identity and class are no longer defined by work ability, but by the freedom of consumption choices. We are all being trained to be consumers throughout our lives: from advertisements to social media, they all imply that the standard of a "decent life" is to be able to afford a house, drive a good car, and follow the trends. The new poor are those who cannot meet these standards; they may have a job, but due to high prices, low wages, or unemployment, their consumption is limited. Poverty is no longer a threat to survival (such as hunger), but a social psychological exclusion: being unable to consume means being marginalized, which triggers shame and guilt. Globally, this "new poverty" is particularly evident in developed cities, reminding us how consumerism has reshaped inequality.

example_sentence.zh: 在社交媒体时代，许多年轻人沦为“新穷人”——他们虽有稳定收入，却因高昂的教育贷款和物价上涨，无法负担结婚或购房，常被嘲笑为“失败者”
example_sentence.en: In the era of social media, many young people have become "new poor" - although they have stable incomes, they are unable to afford marriage or home purchases due to high education loans and rising prices, and are often ridiculed as "losers".

content.zh: 导读
content.en: abstract

content.zh:
首先新穷人是一个系统现象/问题，我认为个人解决的第一步是在自己的日常生活中思考这个现象。如果可以为其发声，可以避免消费主义被无限地合理化。
鲍曼这样形容新穷人的现实后果：由于新穷人是不服从工作伦理的，常常被指责称为道德劣等的人，这使得“穷人的苦难不再能汇聚成一项共同的事业，每一个有缺陷的消费者都在孤独中舔舐自己的伤口，最多只能与ta们尚未破碎的家庭为伴，与同样没有资源的朋友为伴”。
在这里我们可以看到，新穷人的困境一定程度上源自和植根于“沉默”。这是一种系统性的难以发声、难以被理解的沉默。这使得新穷人往往不被识别、被孤立、被怪罪。这就是为什么针对这一现象的提问、反思，对自己日常生活的审视，都是积极的面对方式。
同时我们需要意识到，消费社会如果不能在物理上分隔新穷人，便试图在精神上将其隔绝。在互联网上发出更多声音去反思消费（比如近几年常常有人分享自己在主动寻求消费降级），让新穷人变得更可见，都是有价值的行动。
content.en:
First, the new poor must be understood as a systemic phenomenon and a structural problem. I believe that the first step of individual engagement lies in reflecting on this phenomenon within one’s own everyday life. Giving voice to it, where possible, can prevent consumerism from being endlessly legitimized through rationalization.
Bauman describes the concrete consequences faced by the new poor in the following terms: because the new poor are perceived as deviating from the work ethic, they are frequently accused of moral inferiority. As a result, “the suffering of the poor can no longer crystallize into a common cause; each defective consumer is left to lick their wounds in solitude, accompanied at most by families not yet broken apart, or by friends who are themselves equally deprived of resources.”
Here we can observe that the predicament of the new poor is, to a significant extent, rooted in and sustained by silence—a form of systemically produced silence, characterized by the difficulty of articulation and recognition. This silence renders the new poor largely invisible, socially isolated, and morally blamed.
This is precisely why posing questions about this phenomenon, engaging in reflection, and critically examining one’s own everyday practices constitute active and meaningful forms of response.
At the same time, we must recognize that when consumer society fails to segregate the new poor in physical space, it seeks instead to isolate them on the symbolic and psychological level. Making more voices heard—particularly in digital spaces—to reflect critically on consumption (for example, the growing tendency in recent years to share experiences of deliberate consumption downgrading), and thereby increasing the visibility of the new poor, are actions of genuine value.

brief_definition.zh: 一种生活状态，指人们频繁移动，进行高强度劳动，暂停常规生活，以便快速获益然后迅速逃离
brief_definition.en: A state of life, characterized by frequent movement, intense labor, and suspension of regular life, in order to quickly gain benefits and then quickly escape.

zh: 想象一个年轻的程序员，他从北京搬到深圳，再辗转上海，像一只永不停歇的蜂鸟，在每个城市只停留几个月。白天，他接单做自由职业项目，晚上挤在合租屋里刷招聘网站，只为攒够一笔钱就“逃离”回老家创业。这种生活不是扎根，而是悬在半空——高强度劳动换来短暂收益，却暂停了结婚、买房或社区融入的常规轨迹。

“悬浮”一词，由人类学家项飙提出，描述了现代社会中个体的一种普遍存在状态：人们频繁迁移，进行高强度劳动（如零工经济中的外卖骑手或程序员），主动暂停常规生活（如家庭或社区归属），目的是快速积累财富后迅速“逃离”。这类似于蜂鸟振翅悬停的形象：努力前进却无法着陆，既不批判性参与当下，也不完全脱离。项飙认为，这种状态是发展主义（developmentalism）的缩影——先追求经济收益，问题留待未来解决。它反映了行动者的能动性：一种模糊而脆弱的希望，常被社会结构（如城乡二元制）压制，导致人们反复追问“为什么别无选择？”
在全球零工经济兴起背景下，“悬浮”已成为中国高速发展的隐形引擎。大量农民工或城市白领通过这种状态支撑了服务型经济转型，但也加剧了不平等和环境问题。它像一把双刃剑：短期内维持社会稳定（通过听天由命与希望的混合），长期却可能消解而非解决问题，正如四十年的疯狂发展所暴露的挑战。如今，随着“悬浮”常态化和信念动摇，这个概念正成为社会批判的透镜，揭示行动者在霸权压制下的韧性。
en: Imagine a young programmer who moved from Beijing to Shenzhen, then to Shanghai, like a never-stopping hummingbird, staying in each city for only a few months. During the day, he took on freelance projects, and at night, he crowded in a shared apartment to browse recruitment websites, all in an effort to save enough money to "escape" back to his hometown to start a business. This kind of life is not rooted; it is suspended in mid-air - intense labor yields short-term gains, but it halts the regular trajectory of getting married, buying a house, or integrating into the community.

example_sentence.zh: 在数字游民社群中，许多年轻人选择“悬浮”生活：他们一边在东南亚海滩边远程工作，一边计划着攒够钱就回国创业，却很少思考长期定居的可能
example_sentence.en: Among digital nomads, many embrace "suspension": working remotely on Southeast Asian beaches while plotting entrepreneurial returns home, seldom contemplating permanent settlement.

content.zh: 现在网上流行的暴富崇拜可能也是一种“悬浮”心理的表现？追热点，买彩票，赶风口，期待一夜暴富，期待泼天富贵，我想这些行为折射出的都是对所处社会现实和个体当下生活的不满，但又对改造它无望，所以期待某个天降神力能够把自己从这个泥沼里面拽出来，从此过上别样的生活。我们流行说“赚钱嘛，不嗑颤”，可能也是内心知道这事儿就是挺嗑颤，但追逐财富已经变成了大过一切的绝对正当性，所以也就一边厌恶又一边做着那些迎合的、浮肿的、对伦理问题漠然、自己也不相信它对的事。这种追逐或者“悬浮”即是，好像只要财富自由了，就可以润了溜了颠儿了，所以当下的、此处的、附近的公共文化和公共议题被搁置起来，没有人再相信需要对社会产生价值来获得回报。这是场大病。

“悬浮”这个不算新鲜，跟小蓝交流的时候她也表示这些词，包括内卷、躺平、异化什么的，都被“用到包浆”了。但自从共创会上听小蓝比较成系统地讲了之后，我还是很经常回味“悬浮”这个词的意味，并且产生很多发散的联想。一是它似乎可以被看做是“栖居”的反面：欧洲中世纪人把此世搁置起来，作为赎罪，把幸福美好寄托到来世。对于当代中国语境，那么主教们总对高三学生说：现在辛苦一年，高考完就自由了轻松了。但事实上从小学一年级开始，每一年都被讲作“最关键的一年”，耽误不得，于是一个人不断搁置当下，不断对着先苦后甜的说法充饥。这可能也是一种“悬浮”？另有一种成年人的常见自我pua，自我画饼：“等我xx了我就xx”，最后始终没有充分地活在当下

想补充两个接近于“悬浮”的例子。
一是一种时间上的悬浮，（一直在等待未来）。我的妈妈，一个在没有搬家之前永远属于“悬浮”状态的中年女性。妈妈离婚之后搬进了一个之前的老房子里，老房子即使被翻新了，她依然非常不满意，当我说提一些建议的时候，她总是说：“等这段时间过了多”，“等搬新房子多”，仿佛现在的生活是“暂时”的，这段苦日子总会过去的。
现在她终于搬家了，我说你多久重新开始运动啊?，她说“等春天来了多”…

另外一种是空间上的悬浮，（一直在寻找别处）。是迁徙于被于各种国家间的年轻人，他们通常不想回到自己的国家，但是又同样平等地讨厌每个她们长期呆过的城市和国家，其中我听到辱骂声最多的是德国，每一个在德国长期待的人都仿佛特别憎恨这片土地。

他们（或者是我们）仿佛永远在寻找一块并不存在的 Dream Land，也许扎根质地都是牢笼，所以只能在移动中和未完成种获得一种安全感。

brief_definition.zh: 通过当下涉海行为而非亲属血缘定义的流动身份
brief_definition.en: A fluid identity defined by immediate sea-related actions rather than kinship or descent.

zh: 想象你站在马达加斯加西海岸的沙滩上，看着两个人在海边劳作。其中一人皮肤黝黑、手掌粗茧，但他正弯着腰在小片旱地上拨弄庄稼；另一人则是刚从独木舟上跳下、全身湿透、正熟练地解开缠绕在指缝间的鱼线。对于当地人来说，那一刻，只有后者是“维佐人”，而前者——即便他父母都是维佐人——此时此刻也被视为“内陆人”。

这就是维佐人独特的身份观：身份不是一种“存在状态”（State of being），而是一种“行为方式”（Way of doing）。要被认可为维佐人，不需要查验你的族谱或DNA，只需要观察你当下的行动。如果你像维佐人一样栖海而居、乘风破浪、捕鱼为生，你就是维佐人。这种身份具有极强的“实时性”：一个孩子在学会游泳前只能被称为“小维佐”；一个维佐人如果搬到内陆种地，他在握住锄头的那一刻就不再是维佐人。身份就像是刻在身体上的动态纹章——指尖被鱼线勒出的深痕、为了抓牢沙地而形成的独特步态，都是“做”出来的证明。这种彻底的“获致身份”告诉我们，人不是由他的过去决定的，而是由他正在创造的当下决定的。
en: Imagine standing on the sun-drenched shores of western Madagascar, watching two people at work. One has dark skin and calloused hands but is bent over a small plot of dry land tending to crops; the other has just leapt from an outrigger canoe, dripping wet, skillfully untangling a fishing line caught between his fingers. To the locals, at that exact moment, only the latter is "Vezo," while the former—even if both his parents were born Vezo—is considered an "inlander."

This is the essence of Vezo identity: it is not a "state of being" but a "way of doing." To be recognized as Vezo, one does not need to produce a genealogy or a DNA test; one only needs to be observed in action. If you live by the sea, navigate the waves, and sustain yourself through fishing, you are Vezo. This identity is intensely "real-time": a child is merely a "little Vezo" until they master swimming; a Vezo person who moves inland to farm ceases to be Vezo the moment they grip a hoe. Identity is like a dynamic crest etched upon the body—the deep scars on fingertips from fishing lines and the distinctive gait adapted for gripping sand are all "performed" proofs. This radical "achieved status" suggests that a person is defined not by their past, but by the present they are actively creating.

example_sentence.zh: 在维佐人的哲学里，并没有“一劳永逸”的归属感；这提醒了每一个在大城市里感到迷失的现代人：定义我们的不应是那张薄薄的出生证明，而应是我们每天坚持在做的事情。
example_sentence.en: In Vezo philosophy, there is no such thing as a "once and for all" sense of belonging; this serves as a reminder to every lost soul in the modern metropolis that we are defined not by a birth certificate, but by what we choose to do every day.

content.zh:
生活在马达加斯加西海岸的维佐人的身份通过其当下的行为来定义：生计方式、居住地、定居后所掌握的技能、烙在身上的“标志”等，身份仅在行为发生的当下起效。举例而言，在完全习得游泳、捕鱼等技能之前，维佐人的孩子只能被叫做“小维佐（little Vezo）”，不能被称为“维佐人（Vezo）”；搬到内陆居住却精于独木舟制作的人，在制作独木舟时是维佐人，在劳作于耕地时不是维佐人；海上航行时遇到风浪，奋力使船只航行、抱着船身飘回岸边的是维佐人，瑟瑟发抖、无所作为的不是维佐人。维佐人的身份是一种行为方式，而非一种存在状态。
行为在身体上留下痕迹，身体由此成为身份的表征。要想检验维佐人，也可以看看ta身上的伤疤、走路的姿势。维佐人手上有鱼线勒出的伤痕，没有耕种留下的老茧；出于对沙滩的适应选择用脚尖抓地走路，以至在平地上走路会起水泡。然而表象无法取代行为，如果不延续行动，身体上的痕迹也会逐渐消去。对行动与当下的重视构筑了维佐人的身份认同。在生时，维佐人的身份是一种彻头彻尾的获致身份。如果你我愿意，我们都可以在某一刻成为维佐人。
————
“维佐人”的身份认同方式能够给我们诸多启示——我们是怎样的人或许也可以不依靠血脉和宗族，而是依靠行动。
content.en:
The identity of the Vezo people living along the west coast of Madagascar is defined through their actions in the present: their means of subsistence, place of residence, the skills they acquire after settling, and the “marks” inscribed upon their bodies. Identity is operative only in the moment of action.
For example, before fully mastering skills such as swimming and fishing, Vezo children can only be called “little Vezo,” not “Vezo.” A person who moves inland but excels at making dugout canoes is Vezo while building a canoe, but not Vezo while laboring in the fields. At sea, when a storm arises, those who struggle to keep the boat moving or cling to its hull and drift back to shore are Vezo; those who tremble with fear and do nothing are not Vezo. Vezo identity is thus a mode of action rather than a state of being.
Action leaves traces on the body, and the body in turn becomes a visible index of identity. To recognize a Vezo person, one may look at their scars or the way they walk. Vezo hands bear the cuts left by fishing lines, not the calluses of agricultural labor. Adapted to sandy beaches, they grip the ground with their toes when walking, a habit that causes blisters on flat, hardened surfaces. Yet bodily signs can never replace action itself: without the continuation of practice, such traces gradually fade. It is this emphasis on action and immediacy that constitutes Vezo identity. In life, Vezo identity is entirely an achieved identity. If you or I so choose, we too could become Vezo at a given moment.

content.zh: 在人类学领域，一度被认为已经僵化的亲属关系研究现在正在经历一场复苏，Janet Carsten的《亲属关系之后》（After Kinship）所强调的，是将亲属关系从血缘、谱系与制度结构中“松绑”，转而理解为一种在日常生活中被不断生成、维系和转化的实践过程。维佐人的身份认同方式与这一理论取向高度契合：身份并非先于行动而存在，而是在具体实践中被不断实现。正如 Carsten 所指出的，亲属并不是一种自然事实，而是一种通过共居、劳动、照料与身体经验逐渐“变成的关系”，维佐人的“成为维佐人”同样是一种持续的获致过程。两者都拒绝将社会身份理解为稳定的本质，而是强调行动、身体与当下情境的重要性。唐娜·哈拉维（Donna Haraway）在《留在麻烦中》（Staying with the Trouble）里提出了一个有趣又响亮的口号：“造亲，而非造人！”（Make Kin, Not Babies!）—— 她的意思是，亲属关系不止是血缘关系，而是产生连结的能力，比如说，与机器人成为亲属（AI伴侣）、与动物成为亲属等，都展现了我们并没有被绝对的“原子化”而是被迫开发种种新的社会关系。
content.en:
In anthropology, the study of kinship—once widely regarded as rigid and exhausted—has recently undergone a revival. Janet Carsten’s After Kinship plays a key role in this shift by loosening kinship from blood, genealogy, and formal institutional structures, and instead understanding it as a set of practices continuously generated, maintained, and transformed in everyday life.
The Vezo mode of identity formation closely aligns with this theoretical orientation: identity does not exist prior to action, but is repeatedly realized through concrete practice. As Carsten points out, kinship is not a natural fact, but a relationship that gradually “comes into being” through co-residence, labor, care, and embodied experience. In the same way, “becoming Vezo” is an ongoing process of achievement. Both perspectives reject the notion of social identity as a stable essence, and instead emphasize the importance of action, the body, and the immediacy of the present situation.
Donna Haraway, in Staying with the Trouble, offers a striking and memorable slogan: “Make kin, not babies!” What she means is that kinship is not limited to biological ties, but lies in the capacity to form connections—for example, becoming kin with machines (such as AI companions) or with animals. These forms of relatedness show that we have not been completely reduced to isolated individuals; rather, we are being pushed to invent new kinds of social relations.

brief_definition.zh: 源自同一原始语种并由共同词根演变而来的亲属词汇
brief_definition.en: Kin terms derived from the same proto-language and evolved from a common root

zh: 在一个晴朗的夜晚仰望星空。 如果你身处英国，你会指着那闪烁的光点说 "Star"； 如果你跨过海峡来到德国，当地人会称之为 "Stern"； 如果你穿越时空回到古罗马，你会听到 "Stella"； 如果你再去到古希腊，那里的人们叫它 "Aster"。
这些词为何这样相似？这是因为它们拥有同一个“祖母”——原始印欧语（Proto-Indo-European）中的 h₂stḗr。
这就是“同源词”（Cognates）。它的词源来自拉丁语 cognatus，意为“血脉相连”或“一起出生”。 同源词就像是一个庞大氏族中分散在各地的堂兄弟。几千年前，由于部落迁徙，同一个语言家族分家了。随着时间的推移，原本相同的一个词，在不同的地理环境和发音习惯下，各自演变成了不同的模样，但它们的核心基因（词义和基本音架）依然保留着相似性。
值得注意的是，同源词和外来词（Loanwords）是不同的。比如英语中管寿司叫做Sushi，但这是直接从日语借来的，所以英语和日语中的sushi，两者并不是同源词。
en: Gaze up at the starry sky on a clear night. If you were in Britain, you would point to those twinkling dots and say "Star"; if you crossed the channel to Germany, the locals would call them "Stern"; if you traveled through time to ancient Rome, you would hear "Stella"; and if you visited ancient Greece, the people there would call them "Aster."
Why are these words so similar? It is because they share the same "grandmother"—the Proto-Indo-European (PIE) root h₂stḗr.

These are what we call "Cognates." The term originates from the Latin cognatus, meaning "connected by blood" or "born together." Cognates are like cousins of a vast clan scattered across different lands. Thousands of years ago, due to tribal migrations, a single language family branched out. Over time, the same original word evolved into distinct forms under different geographic environments and phonetic habits; yet, their core genes—their meaning and basic phonetic framework—remain strikingly similar.

It is worth noting that cognates are distinct from loanwords. For instance, the English word for sushi is "sushi," but this was borrowed directly from Japanese. Therefore, "sushi" in English and "sushi" in Japanese are not cognates.

example_sentence.en: For English speakers, learning Spanish is often intuitive because the two languages share a vast number of Cognates, such as "Family" and "Familia."

brief_definition.zh: 源自同一语源但因演变路径不同而产生形态差异的词汇对
brief_definition.en: A pair of words derived from the same etymological source but possessing morphological differences due to divergent evolutionary paths.

zh: 同源异形词就像是在婴儿时期就失散的双胞胎兄弟。哥哥留在了家乡，在原初的环境中长大；弟弟则被送到了国外，经历了一番锤炼后回乡。多年后，当弟弟与哥哥重逢时，尽管他们的基因（词根）完全相同，但外貌、口音和气质（拼写、读音和含义）已经截然不同。
最经典的例子莫过于英语中的 Shirt（衬衫）和 Skirt（裙子）。它们都源自原始日耳曼语的 skurtaz（短衣服）。哥哥 Shirt 是土生土长的古英语词，一直留在英语中演变；而弟弟 Skirt 则随维京人去了北欧，演变为古诺斯语，后来又随着维京人的入侵“回”到了英语中。于是，同一个词根分化成了两个词，分别指代了男人的上衣和女人的下装。

造成这种现象的原因通常是时间和路径的差异。比如Frail 和 Fragile 都来自拉丁语中的Fragilis，但前者已经失掉了原本的“g”，后者却比较完好地保留了原拉丁语词的发音和拼写。 这是因为“哥哥”Frail（脆弱的）离开拉丁语很久了，大约在13-14世纪就通过古法语进入了英语。在漫长的中世纪，原本的辅音 "g" 在几百年的口耳相传中被“磨”掉了； 而“弟弟”Fragile（易碎的），则是后来（约15-17世纪）直接从拉丁语或通过学术著作被“请”回英语的。这种“书面借词”或“学究借词”，较为完好地保留了拉丁语父亲的基因。
en: Doublets are like twin brothers separated in infancy. The elder brother remains at home, growing up in his ancestral environment, while the younger is sent abroad, returning only after a long period of refinement and trial. Years later, when they reunite, despite sharing identical genes (roots), their appearance, accent, and temperament (spelling, pronunciation, and meaning) have become worlds apart.

The most classic example is the pair "Shirt" and "Skirt." Both originate from the Proto-Germanic skurtaz (meaning "short garment"). The elder brother, "Shirt," is a native Old English word that evolved within the language. The younger, "Skirt," traveled to Scandinavia with the Vikings, evolved into Old Norse, and eventually "returned" to English following the Viking invasions. Consequently, the same root diverged into two distinct words, eventually designating a man's upper garment and a woman's lower garment, respectively.

The causes of this phenomenon are typically differences in time and trajectory. For instance, "Frail" and "Fragile" both derive from the Latin fragilis. However, the former has lost its original "g," while the latter preserves the Latin spelling and pronunciation quite well. This is because the "elder brother," "Frail," left Latin centuries ago, entering English via Old French around the 13th or 14th century. Throughout the long Middle Ages, the original consonant "g" was "eroded" through centuries of oral transmission. In contrast, the "younger brother," "Fragile," was "invited" back into English later (around the 15th to 17th century) directly from Latin or through scholarly texts. Such "learned borrowings" or "bookish loanwords" tend to preserve the genes of their Latin father much more intact.

brief_definition.zh: 将外来词以字面意思分部翻译，且参照原有构词原理组装的词
brief_definition.en: A form of translation in which a foreign word is translated part-by-part according to its literal meaning and reassembled based on its original morphological principles

zh: 中文里的“蓝牙”一词译自英文中的“blue-tooth”。“摩天大楼”一词译自“skyscraper”。这些都是典型的“仿译词”。“Blue”是蓝色，“tooth”是牙齿，这个英文单词被拆为两部分，然后两部分被原原本本地译出并重新组装起来。
“仿译词”自身的英文是“calque”，而这个英文是法语外来词。在法语中，calque还有一个意思是“抄绘”。建筑学生熟悉的描图纸、硫酸纸，在法文中即是papier calque。从这个意思上也很容易看出“仿译词”带有的含义——某词在进入另一门语言时，被忠实地誊抄。
en: The Chinese term for "Lanya" is translated from the English "blue-tooth," and "Motian dalou" is translated from "skyscraper." These are quintessential examples of "calques." In the case of "Bluetooth," the English word is bifurcated into "blue" and "tooth"; both components are then translated literally and reassembled in Chinese.

The English word for this phenomenon is "calque," which is itself a loanword from French. In French, calque also carries the meaning of "tracing" or "copying." The tracing paper and vellum so familiar to architecture students are known in French as papier calque. From this etymology, the essence of a "calque" becomes clear—it is a word that, upon entering another language, is faithfully traced and transcribed.

example_sentence.zh:
英文中的brianwash仿译自中文的“洗脑”。
英文中的long time no see仿译自中文的“好久不见”。
汉语中的“超人”仿译自英文中的superman，而后者仿译自德语中的Übermensch，意思是超级的人。
example_sentence.en:
The English word "brainwash" is a calque of the Chinese term xinao (洗脑).
The English phrase "long time no see" is a calque of the Chinese greeting haojiu bujian (好久不见).
The Chinese word chaoren (超人) is a calque of the English "superman," which itself is a calque of the German "Übermensch," meaning a "super-human" or a person who has transcended.

content.zh: loanword is a calque and calque is a loanword. loanword 来自德语 lehnwort 即loan-word 属于仿造词(calque) 而calque 直接借自法语calque 属于借词(loanword)
content.en: "Loanword" is a calque, and "calque" is a loanword. The term "loanword" is derived from the German Lehnwort (literally "loan-word"), making it a calque (a word-for-word translation). Conversely, the term "calque" is borrowed directly from the French calque, making it a loanword (a direct phonetic or morphological borrowing).

content.en: The other day, I discovered that beyond the English term "Middle Kingdom" for China, French also uses "Empire du Milieu" (the Empire of the Middle). By the way, I’d previously heard that "Bluetooth" actually originated from the nickname of an ancient Danish king; this, in turn, led me to realize that many seemingly ordinary, everyday English words are actually derived from historical figures' names.

brief_definition.zh: 将外来词以原来国家的当地语言读音为依据翻译的形式
brief_definition.en: A form of translation in which loanwords are rendered based on their original pronunciation in the source language

zh: 我们从一个词漫长而精彩的流变讲起：古罗马时代，有一群人，他们一无所有，对帝国唯一的贡献就是繁衍后代、提供子嗣（Latin: proles）。这个词在拉丁语中演变为 proletarius，意思是没有财产，通过生育来服务国家的底层人。两千年后，这个词经过马克思主义的重新注解，变成了影响世界的新概念——Proletariat，也就是“无产阶级”。当这个词在20世纪初传入中国时，翻译家们并没有意译它，而是依据读音将其转化为五个汉字：“普罗列塔利亚”。
而有趣的是，“普罗列塔利亚”后来常被简称为“普罗”，在中文语境中，常常以“普罗大众”这一词组出现。
这就是典型的“音译词”（Transliteration，或Phonetic Loanword）诞生过程。它指的是在引入外来概念时，不直接翻译其语义，而是寻找发音相近的汉字来模拟原词的读音。值得注意的是，音译和意译并不互斥，譬如对于这个例子——虽然源自法语/英语的音译，但“普”字在中文里有“普遍”、“普通”之意，“罗”有“网罗”之感，以至于其读音和意涵完美契合，实现了一种美妙的“音义合流”。
同类的精彩案例还有“俱乐部”（Club）。这个词源于英语，经由日语传入中国。在发音上，它模拟了日语中 Club 的读音；在字面上，它又生动地描绘了“一群人聚集在一起快乐”的场景（俱-乐-部）。这种既保留音译形式，又兼顾语义表达的词，常被称为“音义兼译”或“音义对应翻译”。
en: We begin with the long and captivating evolution of a single word. In the era of Ancient Rome, there existed a class of people who possessed nothing; their sole contribution to the Empire was the production of offspring, or proles in Latin. This evolved into the Latin term proletarius, referring to the underclass who served the state only through procreation, devoid of property. Two thousand years later, reinterpreted through a Marxist lens, this word transformed into a world-shaping concept: the Proletariat. When this term reached China in the early 20th century, translators did not seek a semantic equivalent; instead, they rendered it phonetically into five characters: Pu-luo-lie-ta-li-ya (普罗列塔利亚).
Intriguingly, this was later shortened to Puluo (普罗), and in the Chinese context, it frequently appears in the phrase Puluo Dazhong (普罗大众), meaning "the general public" or "the masses."

This is a classic example of the birth of a transliterated loanword (Transliteration or Phonetic Loan). It refers to the practice of introducing a foreign concept not by translating its meaning, but by selecting characters with similar sounds to mimic the original pronunciation. It is worth noting that transliteration and semantic translation are not mutually exclusive. In this case, while the word originated as a phonetic rendering of the French/English term, the character Pu (普) in Chinese carries the meaning of "universal" or "common," and Luo (罗) suggests "to gather" or "encompass." Consequently, the sound and the meaning converged perfectly, achieving a sublime "phonosemantic alignment" (Yin-yi He-liu).

Another brilliant case of this kind is the word for "club": Julebu (俱乐部). Originating from the English "Club," it traveled through Japan before arriving in China. Phonetically, it mimics the Japanese pronunciation of "Club"; literally, however, it vividly depicts a scene where "a group of people gather together in joy" (Ju-Le-Bu). Words that preserve the phonetic form while simultaneously conveying the semantic essence are often referred to as "phonosemantic matchings" or "meaning-reinforced transliterations."

example_sentence.zh:
汉语的“休克”音译自英文中的shock。
英文中的tea音译自汉语（闽南语）中的“茶”（发音接近于te）。
汉语（东北官话）中的“马葫芦”音译自日语中的マンホール（manhoru），后者音译自英文中的manhole（下水道）。
汉语中的“歇斯底里”音译自英文中的hysteria。
汉语中的“引擎”音译自英文中的engine。
example_sentence.en:
The Chinese word xiuke (休克) is a transliteration of the English word "shock."
The English word "tea" is a transliteration of the Chinese word for tea, cha (茶), specifically from the Minnan (Hokkien) dialect, where its pronunciation is close to "te."
In Northeast Mandarin, the word mahulu (马葫芦) is a transliteration of the Japanese "manhōru" (マンホール), which in turn was transliterated from the English word "manhole."
The Chinese word xiesidili (歇斯底里) is a transliteration of the English word "hysteria."
The Chinese word yinqing (引擎) is a transliteration of the English word "engine."

content.zh:
老鸨 bawd
大连-Дальний（达里尼）“远方”；
水门汀（水泥）-cement；
康拜因（联合收割机）- combine；
cheongsam 旗袍（实为“长衫”的发音）；
shanghai（源自“上海”）-绑架…当水手；诱骗；强迫；
马路-macadam road（碎石路，源自英国工程师John McAdam）；
pidgin-混杂语，洋泾浜语（源自中式英文“business”-事儿）；
𨋢-lip1-电梯，粵語造字，源自英文lift
水喉 hose 水龙头
基佬- gaylord
content.en:
Bawd (老鸨): The Chinese term laobao (老鸨) is a phonetic loanword derived from the English "bawd."
Dalian - Dalny (Дальний): The city name "Dalian" traces back to the Russian "Dalny" (Дальний), meaning "the distant place."
Shuimenting (水门汀): A transliteration of the English word "cement."
Kangbaiyin (康拜因): A transliteration of the English word "combine" (as in "combine harvester").
Cheongsam (旗袍): Transliterated from the Cantonese pronunciation of changshan (长衫), meaning "long shirt."
Shanghai (shanghaiing): An English verb derived from the city name "Shanghai," meaning to kidnap or trick someone into serving as a sailor, or more broadly, to coerce or induce someone through underhanded means.
Malu (马路 / "Horse Road"): While appearing to mean "road for horses," it is actually a phonetic adaptation of "macadam road," a type of crushed-stone road surface pioneered by the British engineer John McAdam.
Pidgin (洋泾浜语 / 混杂语): This linguistic term is believed to be derived from the Chinese-English mispronunciation of the word "business."
Lip1 (𨋢): A Cantonese character specifically created to represent the English word "lift" (elevator).
Shuihou (水喉 / "Water Throat"): Used in Cantonese for "faucet" or "tap," derived from the English "hose."
Jilao (基佬): A Cantonese term for "gay," phonetically adapted from the English name/term "Gaylord."

content.zh: 补充一下，可能很多朋友不知道pidgin：洋（yáng）泾（jīng）浜（bāng）语，也叫「混合语（意译）」「皮京语（音译）」「皮钦语（音译）」，是人们在说话的时候，混杂多种语言的一种形式，起初多用于贸易往来。最早的混合语，如中国地方方言与英语混合，非洲地方方言与法语混合等。
content.en: As a supplementary note, many of you might not be familiar with the term "Pidgin": in Chinese, it is known as Yangjingbang (洋泾浜语). It is also referred to as "Mixed Language" (a semantic translation) or "Pijing" and "Piqin" (both phonetic transliterations). Pidgin is a linguistic form that arises when people mix multiple languages during interaction, originally emerging primarily for the purposes of trade. The earliest pidgins were formed through the blending of local dialects with colonial languages—for instance, the fusion of Chinese regional dialects with English, or African local dialects with French.

content.zh: 古力盖是一个青岛特色的音译词，同样也是下水道盖的意思。这个词的来源是古力（德语Gully，下水道）+盖子（中文词）合成。
content.en: Guligai (古力盖) is a transliterated term unique to the Qingdao dialect, also referring to a manhole cover. The word is a hybrid compound consisting of Guli (derived from the German "Gully," meaning sewer or drain) and Gai (the Chinese word for "cover" or "lid").

brief_definition.zh: 强调人的行为、情绪等主观感受的城市空间理解方式
brief_definition.en: An urban spatial understanding emphasizing subjective experiences, such as human act and emotions

zh: 想象你不看导航，在城市中漫步，你所经历的空间并不会像传统地图中绘制的那样展开——快步经过的街道在记忆中迅速淡去，而两个相邻的街区，可能仅仅因为完全不同的建筑风格或光影氛围，在你脑海中显得相隔甚远。如果更本真地根据这段体验绘制地图，那些匆匆走过的街巷将成为空白，而停留更久的街区则会充满细节。

这种对空间的“主观记录”便是心理地理学的核心。不同于传统地理学对物理空间的测量与记录，它试图捕捉不同个体或群体所感受到的空间氛围，以及环境对人情绪的影响。同一座城市会在不同人心中呈现出完全不同的“地理”。深受本雅明“游荡者”这一概念的影响，居伊·德波及其合作者阿斯格·尤恩（Asger Jorn）尝试用更图像化的方式记录对城市的主观体验。在1958年他们创作的巴黎地图中，两人通过剪切、拼贴和红色箭头指向的方式，呈现了在不同空间中穿行以及搭车穿越巴黎街区的感官体验。
en: Imagine wandering through a city without GPS. The space you experience won’t unfold neatly like a traditional map. Streets you rush through might vanish from your memory, while two adjacent blocks could feel miles apart simply because of their different architectural styles or lighting. If you were to draw a map based truly on this lived experience, some parts would remain blank, while other spaces would be dense with detail.

This "subjective recording" of space is at the heart of psychogeography. Moving away from the physical measurements of traditional geography, it seeks to capture the unique atmospheres felt by individuals and the emotional impression of the environment. The same city can manifest as a completely different "geography" in the minds of different people. Influenced by Walter Benjamin’s concept of the flâneur, Guy Debord and his collaborator Asger Jorn sought more graphic ways to document this subjective urban experience. In 1958, they created The Naked City, a psychogeographic map of Paris where they used cut-outs, collages, and directional arrows to map the sensory experience of drifting through different sectors of the city.

example_sentence.zh: 与其查阅冷冰冰的旅游手册，他更倾向于通过一次漫无目的的深夜“漂移”，去书写属于自己的心理地理学报告。
example_sentence.en: Rather than consulting a cold travel brochure, he preferred to write his own psychogeographical report through an aimless late-night "dérive."

caption.zh: 《巴黎心理地理学地图》局部。

content.zh: 导读
content.en: abstract

content.zh:
居伊·德波（Guy Debord）的纪录片《景观社会》（The Society of the Spectacle）存在一种特殊的断裂感：画面缺乏连贯的叙事，充斥着广告、新闻和政治宣传拼贴式的快速剪辑；语调冷漠的旁白与画面之间并没有直接的内容关联，而是直接朗读《景观社会》一书的理论文本。这种“反电影”式的断裂感，似乎正是居伊·德波和情境主义国际（Situationist International，简称SI）所追求的空间体验。
在1957年，几个欧洲激进的前卫团体合并成立了SI，其中包括以居伊·德波为首的“字母主义国际”（Lettrist International）和以阿斯格·约恩（Asger Jorn）为代表的“想象主义包豪斯”（Imaginist Bauhaus）。SI主张将艺术从博物馆和画廊陈列的“物品”的定义中解放出来，他们认为“艺术”应该构建“情境”（Constructed Situations）。所谓情境，就是“通过集体性的环境组织和游戏，创造出一种短暂的、独特的、能让参与者成为主角的生活瞬间”。
在现代城市中，街道被异化为无数“景观”（Spectacle）的堆叠。资本主义不再仅仅生产商品，更生产影像和社会关系。城市本身变成了商品的陈列柜，甚至成为商品本身，而城市生活则是观看和消费。为了对抗这种令人窒息的资本主义景观，情境主义国际构想出了一种游击战式的空间策略——“漂移”（Dérive）。
不同于波德莱尔式“游荡者”（Flâneur）那种忧郁、孤独且旁观式的漫步，情境主义者更像是城市规则的“破坏者”。“漂移”是一种在主观体验上对城市空间进行的暴力剪切与重组，它让那些本被阶级和功能区隔开的街区发生碰撞。这一策略要求参与者彻底抛弃工作、身份和习惯的重负，听从潜意识的召唤，进行一种即兴的、主观的穿越。其目的是在“此时此地”制造陌生感与邂逅的可能，找回现代城市所缺失的不完整性、短暂性和创造性。可以说，“漂移”本质上带有某种狂欢的性质。
1953年的夏天，当整个巴黎依然按照生产的节律运转时，德波和让-米歇尔·曼森（Jean-Michel Mension）发起了一场“不间断的搭便车漂移”。在这场没有终点的旅程中，他们将去向交给随机停下的司机，“快速地穿越不同的氛围”，让原本毫不相关的地理碎片在心理层面发生剧烈碰撞，从而在城市中制造出一种玩乐式的混乱。这种行为本身即是一种宣言：对于深受达达主义和超现实主义影响的左翼国际组织而言，“漂移”构成了瞬间的、艺术性的日常生活革命，以及对资本主义景观的反抗。
相比之下，前段时间流行的“Citywalk”更像是一种对“反叛”的收编和规训。在精心设计的路线图上打卡网红店铺，很难产生漂移的“断裂感”。这种漫步体验本身甚至也被异化为一种可供售卖和消费的商品——曾经对景观的破坏，如今转变成了对景观的再次消费。
